definition_zh: 差距；悬殊；不平等；不一致；差异
definition_en: a clear and often unfair difference in amount, level or treatment between two or more groups or things
core_image: 一条被两端拉开的橡皮尺，刻度越拉越疏，尺子两头各站着一群人
scene: 同一座城市里，两个街区的收入曲线越拉越开，一边不断盖起新楼，一边仍是旧屋。The report measured the widening disparity between the two districts.
sceneCN: 这里指两个群体在收入与发展水平上的明显落差（第 1 个义项：群体之间可测量的差距）；句意为报告测量了两个街区之间不断扩大的差距。图中可辨识物件：两排新旧不同的房屋、一道逐渐变宽的缝隙、一份摊开的报表。

pos.zh: 差距；悬殊；不平等；不一致

derivatives.zh: 同一词干加形容词词尾构成，义为「迥然不同的；不相干的」
由形容词加副词词尾构成，义为「以迥然不同的方式」
由形容词加表示性质的名词词尾构成，义为「互不相同的性质」

senses.title: A measurable gap between groups
senses.titleCN: 群体之间可测量的落差
senses.definition: a difference in amount or level between two groups that can be measured and compared
senses.definitionCN: 两个群体在数量或水平上可以被测量、比较的差别
senses.example: The disparity between urban and rural incomes has drawn public attention.
senses.exampleCN: 城乡收入的差距已经引起公众关注。
senses.why: The Latin word meant simply unequal; the noun keeps that neutral arithmetic sense of two things failing to match.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁词本义就是「不相等」；这个名词保留了「两者对不上」的中性算术含义。

senses.title: Unequal distribution of money
senses.definition: the unequal spread of income, wealth or assets across a population
senses.definitionCN: 收入、财富或资产在一国人口中分配不均
senses.example: Wealth disparity inside the country grew faster than average income.
senses.exampleCN: 该国境内的财富悬殊比平均收入的增长更快。
senses.why: Once the gap is counted in money, the word takes on the policy charge of unfair distribution.
senses.whyCN: 一旦差距用金钱来衡量，这个词就带上了「分配不公」的政策色彩。

senses.title: Regional development imbalance
senses.definition: a persistent difference in prosperity, services or infrastructure between regions
senses.definitionCN: 不同地区在繁荣程度、公共服务或基础设施上的持续差别
senses.example: Regional disparity in hospital funding remains wide.
senses.exampleCN: 各地区在医院拨款上的差距依然很大。
senses.why: The noun was extended from people to places: a map can also be pulled out of shape.
senses.whyCN: 这个词从人群扩展到地方：一张地图同样可以被拉得变形。

senses.title: Gender gap
senses.definition: a difference between men and women in pay, promotion, health or representation
senses.definitionCN: 男女在薪酬、晋升、健康或代表性上的差别
senses.example: The study linked the gender disparity in promotions to biased review criteria.
senses.exampleCN: 这项研究把晋升中的性别差距归因于有偏向的评审标准。
senses.why: Social statistics gave the old word a new pair of columns, one for each sex.
senses.whyCN: 社会统计给这个旧词添了一对新栏目，男女各占一栏。

senses.title: Racial and ethnic difference
senses.definition: a difference in outcomes or treatment that falls along racial or ethnic lines
senses.definitionCN: 结果或待遇上沿种族、族裔界线出现的差别
senses.example: Racial disparity in school discipline has been documented for decades.
senses.exampleCN: 学校纪律处分中的种族差异已被记录了数十年。
senses.why: Where the two groups are named by race or ethnicity, the neutral gap becomes evidence of unequal treatment.
senses.whyCN: 当两组人按种族或族裔来命名时，中性的落差就变成了待遇不公的证据。

senses.title: Health outcome gap
senses.definition: a difference in illness, access to care or life expectancy between populations
senses.definitionCN: 不同人群在患病率、就医机会或预期寿命上的差别
senses.example: Health disparity between insured and uninsured patients widened during the epidemic.
senses.exampleCN: 传染病流行期间，有保险与无保险患者之间的健康差距扩大了。
senses.why: Medicine borrowed the word to describe bodies that receive unequal care, not unequal numbers.
senses.whyCN: 医学借用了这个词，用来描述得到不平等照护的身体，而不是不平等的数字。

senses.title: Unequal access to opportunity
senses.definition: an uneven chance to obtain schooling, jobs or advancement
senses.definitionCN: 获得教育、工作或上升通道的机会不均等
senses.example: Educational disparity begins before children enter school.
senses.exampleCN: 教育机会的差距在孩子入学之前就已开始。
senses.why: The gap is no longer a result but a starting line drawn in different places.
senses.whyCN: 这时的差距不再是结果，而是一条画在不同位置上的起跑线。

senses.title: Numerical inconsistency in records
senses.titleCN: 数据记录上的数值不一致
senses.definition: a failure of two sets of figures to agree with each other
senses.definitionCN: 两套数字彼此对不上
senses.example: Auditors found a disparity between the two ledgers.
senses.exampleCN: 审计人员发现两份账簿之间存在对不上的数字。
senses.why: The oldest sense of unequal survives in bookkeeping, where two columns should have matched.
senses.whyCN: 「不相等」最古老的含义在记账中留存下来：两栏数字本应相符。

senses.title: Difference in treatment
senses.definition: an unequal standard applied to people who are in comparable positions
senses.definitionCN: 对处境相当的人适用不同标准
senses.example: Employees complained of disparity in overtime pay.
senses.exampleCN: 员工抱怨加班费的发放标准悬殊。
senses.why: When the comparison moves from amounts to rules, disparity means one rule for two similar people.
senses.whyCN: 当比较从数量转向规则，这个词就指对两个相似的人用了两套标准。

intro.en: Latin gives disparity a clean line: a negative prefix, a root meaning equal, and a noun of state. English took the noun through French and later loaded it with social statistics.
intro.cn: 拉丁语为这个词提供了清楚的线索：一个否定前缀、一个表示「相等」的词根，以及一个表状态的名词词尾。英语经法语借入该名词，后来又让它承担社会统计的含义。

items.en: par meant equal, a match, a pair; it named things that stand level with one another.
items.cn: par 意为「相等、对等、一对」，指彼此齐平的事物。

items.en: dis- marked separation or negation, so dispar described a pair that does not stand level.
items.cn: dis- 表示分开或否定，因此 dispar 描述一对站不平齐的事物。

items.en: The abstract noun disparitas named the state itself: inequality, unlikeness.
items.cn: 抽象名词 disparitas 直接命名这种状态：不相等、不相同。

items.en: Middle French carried the noun forward, and English borrowed it in the sixteenth century.
items.cn: 中世纪法语把这个名词继续传下去，英语在十六世纪借入。

items.en: The first English record is dated to the sixteenth century; the exact year is not certain, but the source line itself is not in dispute.
items.cn: 英语首见记录可定在十六世纪；具体年份不确定，但来源线索本身没有争议。

items.en: Twentieth-century social science attached the word to income, gender, race, health and regional columns.
items.cn: 二十世纪社会科学把这个词挂到收入、性别、种族、健康与地区这些栏目上。

note.en: The first group shares shape or root with disparity; the second group names neighbouring ideas of a gap or a mismatch.
note.cn: 第一组在形音或词根上与 disparity 相近；第二组是与「落差、对不上」意思相邻的说法。

entries.definition: An adjective meaning markedly different or not comparable; it is the quality behind the noun.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「迥然不同的、不可比的」，正是这个名词背后的性质。

entries.definition: Equality of level or status; it is the positive counterpart built on the same root for equal.
entries.definitionCN: 指水平或地位相等；是同一「相等」词根构成的正面反义对应词。

entries.definition: To speak of someone or something as of little value; it looks close but came through a French verb about lowering rank, not from the unequal pair.
entries.definitionCN: 指贬低某人或某物；形近，但来自法语表示「降低门第」的动词，并非出自「不相等」这一对词。

entries.definition: The plural form used when several gaps are counted together.
entries.definitionCN: 复数形式，用于把多处差距合在一起计数。

entries.definition: An unfair difference in status, wealth or opportunity; broader and more political than a measured gap.
entries.definitionCN: 指地位、财富或机会上的不公平差别；比一个可测量的落差更宽泛，也更带政治色彩。

entries.definition: The open distance between two levels or groups; plainer and less formal.
entries.definitionCN: 指两个水平或群体之间的空档；更朴素，也更口语。

entries.definition: A lack of proportion between parts, often suggesting something needs correcting.
entries.definitionCN: 指各部分比例失调，常暗示需要纠正。

entries.definition: A failure of two accounts or figures to agree; it stresses contradiction rather than social distance.
entries.definitionCN: 指两份说法或数字对不上；强调矛盾，而非社会性落差。

entries.definition: A failure of statements or figures to agree with one another; it is a mismatch in consistency, not a measured gap between groups.
entries.definitionCN: 指说法或数字彼此对不上；它是「是否一致」的失配，而不是群体之间可测量的落差。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations use the real parts dis- and par, the real sister words parity and peer, and real statistical phrases.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想使用真实的构词部件 dis- 与 par、真实的同根词 parity 与 peer，以及真实的统计搭配。

normal.en: dis- means apart, par means equal: pull equal things apart and you have a disparity.
normal.cn: dis- 表示分开，par 表示相等：把相等的东西拉开，就有了差距。

normal.en: Parity and peer share the same root, so disparity is the unequal twin of equality.
normal.cn: parity 与 peer 同根，因此 disparity 是「平等」那个词的不平等双胞胎。

normal.en: Picture a balance scale with one pan resting lower: that tilt is the gap.
normal.cn: 想象一架天平，一边盘子垂得更低：那份倾斜就是差距。

normal.en: Income disparity, gender disparity and health disparity are three real policy phrases.
normal.cn: 收入差距、性别差距与健康差距是三个真实的政策说法。

normal.en: Two columns of statistics sit side by side; disparity is the distance between them.
normal.cn: 两列统计数字并排而立；差距就是两列之间的距离。

abstract.en: A gap is not a wall: it is a distance that can be measured and therefore can be closed.
abstract.cn: 落差不是一堵墙，而是一段可以测量、因而也可以弥合的距离。

abstract.en: Every average hides a disparity: the mean is a line, and the gap is the space around it.
abstract.cn: 每一个平均值都藏着一处落差：均值是一条线，落差是线周围的空间。

abstract.en: Disparity is inequality turned into a number, which is why it can be argued about.
abstract.cn: 差距是被换算成数字的不平等，所以它才可以被争论。

examples.en: The survey found a sharp disparity between what men and women earn for the same work.
examples.cn: 调查发现，男女做同样的工作，报酬却有明显差距。

examples.en: Regional disparity in school funding has narrowed since the new formula was adopted.
examples.cn: 自从采用新的拨款公式，各地区的学校教育经费差距已经缩小。

examples.en: A disparity of two units between the inventories delayed the shipment.
examples.cn: 两份库存清单上有两个单位的出入，导致发货延迟。

dict_mnemonic.text: 读作「迪斯帕若提」——把「相等」分开，剩下的就是差距

root: 来自拉丁语 disparitas「不相等」← dispar「不相等的」，由 dis-「分开、不」与 par「相等」构成，经中世纪法语 disparité 进入英语。词源链清楚，仅首见年代为约数。

sensesIntro.en: Nine senses run from a neutral measured gap through money, regions, gender, race, health and opportunity to records and treatment.
sensesIntro.cn: 九个义项从一个中性的可测落差出发，经过金钱、地区、性别、种族、健康与机会，最后落到账目与待遇。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: one rubber ruler is pulled wider at one end, and its marks drift apart.
core.cn: 核心意象：一把橡皮尺的一端被拉宽，刻度随之越走越疏。

branches.en: THE NEUTRAL MEASURE: two groups simply fail to match on the same scale.
branches.cn: 中性的测量：两个群体在同一把尺子上就是对不上。

branches.en: THE MONEY AND THE MAP: income distribution and regional development pull apart.
branches.cn: 钱与地图：收入分配和地区发展各自被拉开。

branches.en: THE BODY AND THE GROUP: gender, race and health outcomes carry the gap into daily life.
branches.cn: 身体与群体：性别、种族与健康结果把落差带进日常生活。

branches.en: THE STARTING LINE: schooling and opportunity begin at different points.
branches.cn: 起跑线：教育与机会从不同的位置开始。

branches.en: THE LEDGER AND THE PAY SLIP: figures that disagree and rules applied unevenly.
branches.cn: 账簿与工资单：对不上的数字，以及适用不均的规则。

intro.en: Disparity is built from a negative prefix, a root meaning equal, and a noun ending of state.
intro.cn: 这个词由一个否定前缀、一个表示「相等」的词根和一个表状态的名词词尾构成。

latinIntro.en: Latin supplies par, dispar and disparitas; parity is the positive noun from the same root.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语提供了 par、dispar 与 disparitas；parity 是同根词构成的正面名词。

items.example: It turns equal into unequal.
items.exampleCN: 它把「相等」变成「不相等」。

items.example: The root names things that stand level.
items.exampleCN: 这个词根命名彼此齐平的事物。

items.example: The prefix and root first meet here.
items.exampleCN: 前缀与词根在这里首次结合。

items.example: The abstract noun adds a state ending.
items.exampleCN: 这个抽象名词加上表状态词尾。

items.example: It turns the adjective into the English noun.
items.exampleCN: 它把形容词变成英语名词。

items.example: It forms disparate, the adjective of difference.
items.exampleCN: 它构成表示差异的形容词 disparate。

items.example: The positive counterpart of disparity.
items.exampleCN: 是 disparity 的正面对应词。

items.example: The same root survives in the word for an equal.
items.exampleCN: 同一词根在表示「同等者」的词里留存。

items.example: The plural marks more than one measured gap.
items.exampleCN: 复数标记不止一处可测的落差。

derivatives.zh: 由词干加形容词词尾构成，义为「迥然不同的」
由形容词加副词词尾构成，义为「以不同方式」
由形容词加名词词尾构成，义为「互不相同的性质」

definition_zh: 开发利用；资源开采；商业开发；剥削；利用；漏洞利用
definition_en: the act of using a resource, situation or person for profit or advantage, whether fairly and productively or unfairly and at their expense
core_image: 一座山被层层剥开，矿石装上卡车运走，山脚下的人只拿到很少的报酬
scene: 矿区的老照片挂在会议室墙上，一边是装满矿石的卡车，一边是被挖空的山体。The company's exploitation of the local iron ore lasted forty years.
sceneCN: 这里指对自然资源的开采利用（第 1 个义项：资源开发利用）；句意为这家公司对当地铁矿的开发持续了四十年。图中可辨识物件：露天矿坑、运矿卡车、山体剖面、会议室照片墙。

pos.zh: 开发利用；资源开采；剥削；利用

derivatives.zh: 同一词干构成的动词与名词，义为「开发利用；剥削」与「功绩」
由动词加表示施动者的名词尾构成，义为「开发者；剥削者」
由动词加表示性质的形容词尾构成，义为「剥削性的」
由动词加表示「可……的」形容词尾构成，义为「可利用的」
由表示「过度」的前缀加本词构成，义为「过度开发」

senses.title: Productive use of natural resources
senses.definition: the working of land, minerals, water or forests for economic benefit
senses.definitionCN: 对土地、矿产、水源或森林进行有经济收益的开发利用
senses.example: The company's exploitation of the local iron ore lasted forty years.
senses.exampleCN: 这家公司对当地铁矿的开发持续了四十年。
senses.why: The oldest sense is a deed carried out and brought to profit, so working a mine counts as an exploit before it counts as abuse.
senses.whyCN: 最古老的含义是「做成一件事并从中获利」，因此开采矿山先被算作一番作为，之后才被算作剥削。

senses.title: Commercial development of an idea or market
senses.definition: the turning of an invention, brand or market into a source of revenue
senses.definitionCN: 把发明、品牌或市场变成收入来源
senses.example: Critics said the film was a commercial exploitation of a true story.
senses.exampleCN: 批评者说这部电影是对一个真实故事的商业开发。
senses.why: When the resource is an idea or a market rather than a mine, the same word means packaging it for sale.
senses.whyCN: 当被开发的对象从矿山变成创意或市场，同一个词就指把它包装出售。

senses.title: Use of data or personal information
senses.titleCN: 数据与个人信息的利用
senses.definition: the collection and use of data, often without the clear consent of the people concerned
senses.definitionCN: 收集并使用数据，且常常没有获得当事人的明确同意
senses.example: The inquiry examined the exploitation of user data by the platform.
senses.exampleCN: 调查审查了该平台对用户数据的使用。
senses.why: Data became a resource in the digital economy, and the word followed the resource.
senses.whyCN: 在数字经济中数据成了资源，这个词也就跟着资源走。

senses.title: Unfair use of labour
senses.definition: the payment of very little for long or hard work while another party keeps the profit
senses.definitionCN: 以极低报酬换取长时间或高强度劳动，利润归他方所有
senses.example: Inspectors found exploitation of migrant workers on the construction site.
senses.exampleCN: 检查人员发现工地上存在对移民工人的剥削。
senses.why: Here the thing being worked is a person, and the profit is taken from their hours and body.
senses.whyCN: 这里被「开发」的对象是人，利润取自他们的工时与身体。

senses.title: Taking advantage of generosity
senses.definition: the use of someone's kindness, trust or weakness for one's own benefit
senses.definitionCN: 利用他人的善意、信任或弱点为自己谋利
senses.example: He described the loan as an exploitation of his father's generosity.
senses.exampleCN: 他把这笔借款说成是对父亲善意的利用。
senses.why: No mine and no market are needed: a human weakness is the seam being excavated.
senses.whyCN: 既不需要矿山也不需要市场：被开采的矿脉是人的弱点。

senses.title: Abuse of a vulnerable group
senses.definition: a systematic taking of value from people who cannot refuse, such as children or the poor
senses.definitionCN: 从无法拒绝的人身上系统性地榨取价值，如儿童或穷人
senses.example: The report documented exploitation of children in the informal economy.
senses.exampleCN: 报告记录了大量非正规经济中对儿童的剥削。
senses.why: The word turns from individual meanness to a structure when the group itself has no power to say no.
senses.whyCN: 当整个群体没有拒绝的能力时，这个词就从个人的刻薄变成一种结构。

senses.title: Extraction beyond renewal
senses.titleCN: 超出再生能力的过度攫取
senses.definition: harvesting or extraction at a rate faster than a natural system can recover
senses.definitionCN: 采伐或捕捞的速度快过自然系统的恢复能力
senses.example: Over-exploitation of the fishery left the boats with empty nets.
senses.exampleCN: 对渔场的过度捕捞让渔船空手而归。
senses.why: The prefix of excess turns the same act into one that destroys its own resource.
senses.whyCN: 表示「过度」的前缀把同一行为变成毁掉自身资源的行为。

senses.title: Use of a technical flaw
senses.definition: the deliberate use of a weakness in software or a system to gain access or control
senses.definitionCN: 故意利用软件或系统中的弱点取得访问权或控制权
senses.example: The attack began with exploitation of an unpatched browser flaw.
senses.exampleCN: 这次攻击始于对一个未修补的浏览器漏洞的利用。
senses.why: A loophole is a resource too: security language borrowed the word for a hole opened on purpose.
senses.whyCN: 漏洞也是一种资源：安全领域借用了这个词，指一个被故意打开的缺口。

senses.title: Full use of an opportunity
senses.definition: the energetic use of a chance or advantage that is legitimately available
senses.definitionCN: 对一个正当可用的机会或优势加以充分利用
senses.example: The coach praised the team's exploitation of every scoring chance.
senses.exampleCN: 教练称赞球队充分利用了每一次得分机会。
senses.why: The neutral sense survives in sport and business, where using an opening well is simply good play.
senses.whyCN: 这个中性含义在体育与商业中留存：把空档用好，本身就是好球。

intro.en: Exploitation goes back to a Latin verb meaning to unfold, through French a deed or a profit, and then to the modern sense of working a resource.
intro.cn: 这个词可追到拉丁语表示「展开」的动词，经法语表示「作为、获利」，再到现代「开发资源」的含义。

items.en: plicare meant to fold, and its compounds describe bending something into layers.
items.cn: plicare 意为「折叠」，其复合词描述把某物折成层。

items.en: ex- plus plicare gave explicare, to unfold or set out in order.
items.cn: 表示「向外」的前缀加「折叠」，构成 explicare，意为「展开、摊开说明」。

items.en: The participle explicitum named something unfolded and therefore made clear.
items.cn: 分词形式 explicitum 指被展开、因而变得清楚的事物。

items.en: French turned the idea into esploit, a deed accomplished, and later a source of profit.
items.cn: 法语把这一意思变成 esploit，指做成的一番作为，后来指利润来源。

items.en: English first used the deed word as exploit and built exploitation on it; the first records cluster in the early modern period and the exact date is uncertain.
items.cn: 英语先把「作为」这个词用作 exploit，再由此构成 exploitation；首见记录集中出现在近代早期，具体年份不确定。

items.en: Industrial mining and factory labour gave the noun its double life as resource development and human abuse.
items.cn: 工业化采矿与工厂劳动让这个名词有了双面人生：资源开发与对人的剥削。

note.en: The first group shares form or root with exploitation; the second group names nearby ideas of using something for gain.
note.cn: 第一组在形音或词根上与 exploitation 相近；第二组是与「为获利而使用」意思相邻的说法。

entries.definition: The verb to develop a resource or take unfair advantage of a person, and the noun for a bold deed.
entries.definitionCN: 指开发资源或对人占便宜的动词，也指「壮举」的名词。

entries.definition: A person or firm that works a resource or takes advantage of others.
entries.definitionCN: 指开发资源的个人或企业，或占他人便宜的人。

entries.definition: Describing a relationship or practice that extracts value unfairly.
entries.definitionCN: 形容不公平榨取价值的关系或做法。

entries.definition: The search for resources or knowledge; it looks close but comes from a verb meaning to search out, not to unfold.
entries.definitionCN: 指对资源或知识的勘探与探索；形近，但来自表示「搜寻」而非「展开」的动词。

entries.definition: Stated fully and leaving nothing folded away; it shares the unfolding image.
entries.definitionCN: 指表述完整、毫不含糊；与本词共享「展开」的意象。

entries.definition: The process of bringing land, resources or ideas into productive use; neutral and often positive.
entries.definitionCN: 指把土地、资源或想法带入生产用途的过程；中性且常为正面。

entries.definition: The effective use of something available; it stresses use, not profit or harm.
entries.definitionCN: 指对可用之物的有效使用；强调使用，不强调获利或伤害。

entries.definition: The wrong or harmful use of a power, substance or person; it stresses harm rather than extraction.
entries.definitionCN: 指对权力、物质或人的错误有害使用；强调伤害而非榨取。

entries.definition: Taking plants, fish or animals faster than they can replenish; the ecological twin of over-exploitation.
entries.definitionCN: 指对植物、鱼或动物的捕捞采集快于其补充；是「过度开发」的生态学说法。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations use the real Latin image of unfolding, the real French deed word and the real resource-and-labour pairs.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想使用真实的拉丁「展开」意象、真实的法语「作为」词，以及真实的资源与劳动搭配。

normal.en: The root picture is unfolding: a mine is land unfolded and spread out for profit.
normal.cn: 词根的意象是「展开」：矿山就是被摊开来换钱的土地。

normal.en: French esploit meant a deed done; exploitation is that deed turned into a business.
normal.cn: 法语 esploit 指做成一件事；exploitation 就是这件作为变成了生意。

normal.en: The same word covers a mine and a worker because both are seams someone works.
normal.cn: 同一个词既指矿山又指工人，因为两者都是被人开采的矿脉。

normal.en: Resource exploitation and labour exploitation sit on one page of the dictionary.
normal.cn: 资源开发与劳动剥削在词典的同一页上。

normal.en: Data is the new seam: data exploitation repeats the mining image.
normal.cn: 数据是新的矿脉：数据利用重复了采矿的意象。

abstract.en: Exploitation begins when a thing with its own life is seen only as something to be taken from.
abstract.cn: 剥削始于把一个有自己的生命的东西，只看成可供取用之物。

abstract.en: The word is neutral until the second party cannot say no; then development becomes extraction.
abstract.cn: 这个词本中性，直到另一方无法说不，开发就变成了榨取。

abstract.en: Every loophole is a small hole opened on purpose, which is why security borrowed the mining word.
abstract.cn: 每一个漏洞都是一个被故意打开的小口，所以安全领域借用了采矿的词。

examples.en: The treaty set limits on the exploitation of the river for hydropower.
examples.cn: 该条约对这条河的水电开发设定了限制。

examples.en: The court treated the long unpaid internships as exploitation of young workers.
examples.cn: 法院把长期无薪实习视为对年轻劳动者的剥削。

examples.en: Security teams patched the flaw before exploitation of it became widespread.
examples.cn: 安全团队在漏洞被广泛利用之前就完成了修补。

dict_mnemonic.text: 读作「爱克斯普洛伊泰申」——把矿藏「展开」摊开，再从中取利

root: 来自拉丁语 explicare「展开、摊开说明」← ex-「向外」+ plicare「折叠」，分词 explicitum 指「展开的」；经古法语 esploit「作为、获利」与法语 exploiter 进入英语，再由动词构成 exploitation。首见年代为约数，来源链清楚。

sensesIntro.en: Nine senses move from working a mine, a market, data and a person to passing the limit and to two neutral uses in security and sport.
sensesIntro.cn: 九个义项从开采矿山、开发市场、利用数据和剥削人，走到越过限度，最后落到安全与体育里两个中性用法。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a hillside is unfolded layer by layer, ore goes one way and people stay at the pit edge.
core.cn: 核心意象：山坡被一层层展开，矿石被运走，人留在矿坑边缘。

branches.en: THE LAND AND THE MARKET: ore, land and ideas turned into revenue.
branches.cn: 土地与市场：矿石、土地与创意被换成收入。

branches.en: THE DATA SEAM: records mined for value, often without consent.
branches.cn: 数据矿脉：记录被开采出价值，常常未经同意。

branches.en: THE PERSON AS RESOURCE: hours, kindness and weakness turned into another's gain.
branches.cn: 把人当资源：工时、善意与弱点变成他人的收益。

branches.en: THE LIMIT PASSED: harvest that outruns renewal and destroys the seam.
branches.cn: 越过限度：收割快过再生，最终毁掉矿脉本身。

branches.en: THE OPEN HOLE: a system flaw or a brief chance used to the full.
branches.cn: 敞开的缺口：系统漏洞或短暂机会被充分利用。

intro.en: Exploitation is a verb stem plus a noun ending, with a Latin prefix and a Latin root still visible inside.
intro.cn: 这个词是动词词干加名词词尾，内部仍能看见一个拉丁前缀与一个拉丁词根。

latinIntro.en: Latin supplies plicare and explicare, and the participle explicitum; French supplies the deed word exploit.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语提供了 plicare、explicare 与分词 explicitum；法语提供了表示「作为」的 exploit。

items.example: It marks the unfolding outward.
items.exampleCN: 它标记「向外展开」。

items.example: The root names folded layers.
items.exampleCN: 这个词根命名折叠的层。

items.example: Prefix and root combine into the key verb.
items.exampleCN: 前缀与词根合成关键动词。

items.example: The participle supplies the clear sense.
items.exampleCN: 分词提供了「清楚」的含义。

items.example: It forms the English action noun.
items.exampleCN: 它构成英语的动作名词。

items.meaning: to work for gain; a bold deed
items.example: The base word keeps both sides.
items.exampleCN: 基础词兼含两面。

items.example: It forms exploiter, the one who works the seam.
items.exampleCN: 它构成 exploiter，指开采矿脉的人。

items.example: It forms exploitative, the unfair kind.
items.exampleCN: 它构成 exploitative，指剥削性的。

items.example: It forms exploitable, able to be used.
items.exampleCN: 它构成 exploitable，指可利用的。

derivatives.zh: 由动词加施动者词尾构成，义为「开发者；剥削者」
由动词加性质形容词尾构成，义为「剥削性的」
由动词加「可……的」形容词尾构成，义为「可利用的」
由「过度」前缀加本词构成，义为「过度开发」

definition_zh: 不一致；前后矛盾；反复无常；不稳定；不协调之处
definition_en: the quality of not staying the same, or a case in which statements, figures, standards or behaviour fail to agree with one another
core_image: 两页文件摊在桌上，左边写上升，右边表格却写下降，一支笔停在中缝
scene: 同一份报告里，第一页说销量上升，最后一页的表格却显示下降，编辑在两页之间来回核对。A single inconsistency between the summary and the table delayed the report.
sceneCN: 这里指同一份材料内部前后对不上（第 1 个义项：说法前后不一致）；句意为摘要与表格之间的一处矛盾让报告延期。图中可辨识物件：两页报告、上升与下降的折线、停在中间的一支笔。

pos.zh: 不一致；前后矛盾；反复无常；不稳定

derivatives.zh: 由否定前缀加「一致」形容词构成，义为「不一致的；反复无常的」
由形容词加副词词尾构成，义为「不一致地」
去掉否定前缀后的正面名词，义为「一致性；连贯性」
同一词根的基础动词，义为「由……组成；在于」

senses.title: A statement that contradicts another
senses.definition: a case in which one statement, page or claim does not agree with another from the same source
senses.definitionCN: 同一来源的一处说法、一页或一项主张与另一处对不上
senses.example: A single inconsistency between the summary and the table delayed the report.
senses.exampleCN: 摘要与表格之间的一处矛盾让报告延期。
senses.why: The negative prefix denies standing together: two statements that should stand as one fail to line up.
senses.whyCN: 否定前缀否定了「站在一起」：本应合成一体的两句话没能对齐。

senses.title: Figures that fail to agree
senses.definition: a mismatch between two sets of numbers, records or measurements
senses.definitionCN: 两组数字、记录或测量结果彼此不符
senses.example: The audit flagged an inconsistency in the quarterly accounts.
senses.exampleCN: 审计指出季度账目中存在数字不一致。
senses.why: Bookkeeping is where the word is most concrete: the columns ought to balance and do not.
senses.whyCN: 记账是这个词最具体的地方：两栏本应平衡，却没有平衡。

senses.title: A contradiction inside an argument
senses.definition: a logical conflict between two parts of the same reasoning
senses.definitionCN: 同一套推理的两个部分之间出现逻辑冲突
senses.example: The reviewer pointed out an inconsistency in the paper's central argument.
senses.exampleCN: 审稿人指出论文核心论证中存在一处矛盾。
senses.why: Logic asks whether propositions can stand together; when they cannot, the charge is inconsistency.
senses.whyCN: 逻辑要问几个命题能否站在一起；站不住时，指控就是「不一致」。

senses.title: Uneven quality between batches
senses.definition: a variation in standard or quality from one production run to another
senses.definitionCN: 不同生产批次在标准或质量上的波动
senses.example: Customers reported inconsistency in the thickness of the panels.
senses.exampleCN: 客户反映板材厚度不稳定。
senses.why: Industry applies the word to output: a product that should be identical comes out slightly different each time.
senses.whyCN: 工业界把这个词用于产出：本应一模一样的产品，每次出来都略有不同。

senses.title: Erratic behaviour in a person
senses.definition: a tendency to act in ways that do not match one's earlier words or habits
senses.definitionCN: 一个人的行为与其先前言辞或习惯对不上
senses.example: His inconsistency in keeping promises cost him the team's trust.
senses.exampleCN: 他屡屡不守承诺，失去了团队的信任。
senses.why: A person, not just a sentence, can fail to stand together over time.
senses.whyCN: 不只是句子，一个人随时间推移也可能「站不成一体」。

senses.title: Standards applied unevenly
senses.definition: a failure to apply the same rule or measure in comparable cases
senses.definitionCN: 在可比的情形中没有适用同一规则或尺度
senses.example: Small firms complained about inconsistency in how the tax rules were enforced.
senses.exampleCN: 小企业抱怨税规的执行口径不一致。
senses.why: When two similar cases receive different treatment, the inconsistency lies in the system, not in a sentence.
senses.whyCN: 当两个相似情形受到不同对待，不一致就在制度里，而不在一句话里。

senses.title: A jarring shift in style or narrative
senses.titleCN: 文体或叙述上的不协调
senses.definition: an abrupt change of tone, style or detail that breaks the unity of a text
senses.definitionCN: 语气、风格或细节的突然变化破坏了文本的统一
senses.example: The editor removed the inconsistency in tone between the two chapters.
senses.exampleCN: 编辑删去了两章之间语气上的不协调。
senses.why: A text is expected to hold one voice; a sudden change makes the reader feel the seam.
senses.whyCN: 文本本应保持一种声音；突然的转变让读者感到那道接缝。

senses.title: Uneven performance over time
senses.definition: a rise and fall in results that prevents a steady level from being reached
senses.definitionCN: 成绩忽高忽低，无法达到稳定水平
senses.example: The coach blamed the team's inconsistency on a thin bench.
senses.exampleCN: 教练把球队表现起伏归因于替补阵容单薄。
senses.why: Sport borrowed the word for a player who is brilliant one week and absent the next.
senses.whyCN: 体育借用了这个词，指一周出彩、下一周消失的球员。

senses.title: A specific mismatched detail
senses.definition: one concrete point at which two accounts, descriptions or records differ
senses.definitionCN: 两份陈述、描述或记录在某个具体点上不同
senses.example: Investigators found one clear inconsistency in the witness's account.
senses.exampleCN: 调查人员发现证人陈述中有一处明显的不符。
senses.why: The countable use turns the abstract quality into one concrete point of mismatch.
senses.whyCN: 可数用法把这个抽象性质收拢为一个具体的错位点。

intro.en: Inconsistency is a Latin verb for standing firm, given a negative prefix and a noun ending; the picture is two things that ought to stand together but do not.
intro.cn: 这个词来自拉丁语表示「站稳」的动词，加上否定前缀与名词词尾；意象是两样本应站在一起却站不住的东西。

items.en: sistere meant to cause to stand, to set, to hold one's ground.
items.cn: sistere 意为「使站立、放置、守住位置」。

items.en: con- meant together, so consistere was to stand together, to hold firm, to consist of.
items.cn: con- 表示「一起」，因此 consistere 意为「站在一起、稳固、由……构成」。

items.en: The abstract noun named the state of standing together, hence coherence.
items.cn: 抽象名词命名「站在一起」的状态，也就是连贯一致。

items.en: English built consistency on the Latin noun, first in the sense of firmness and later of agreement.
items.cn: 英语在该拉丁名词上构成 consistency，先指坚固，后指一致。

items.en: Adding the negative prefix denied the standing together, and inconsistency was born as its exact opposite.
items.cn: 加上否定前缀就否定了「站在一起」，inconsistency 作为它的精确反义词出现。

items.en: Statistics and manufacturing gave the word its countable, technical life: mismatched figures and uneven batches.
items.cn: 统计学与制造业赋予它可数的技术生命：对不上的数字与不稳定的批次。

note.en: The first group shares root or form with inconsistency; the second group names nearby ideas of things not matching.
note.cn: 第一组在词根或形音上与 inconsistency 相近；第二组是与「对不上」意思相邻的说法。

entries.definition: The adjective describing a statement, result or person that fails to stay in line.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，形容说法、结果或人无法保持一致。

entries.definition: The positive noun for coherence and steadiness; the exact antonym of this word.
entries.definitionCN: 指连贯与稳定的正面名词，正是本词的反义对应词。

entries.definition: The base verb meaning to be made up of, or to lie in something.
entries.definitionCN: 基础动词，意为「由……组成」或「在于」。

entries.definition: The act of demanding something firmly; it shares the standing root but uses in- as a prefix of pressure, not negation.
entries.definitionCN: 指坚决要求的行为；与「站立」词根同源，但前缀表示施压而非否定。

entries.definition: A failure of two accounts or figures to agree; narrower and more factual than inconsistency.
entries.definitionCN: 指两份说法或数字对不上；比本词更窄、更偏事实。

entries.definition: Two statements that cannot both be true; it stresses logical conflict rather than unevenness.
entries.definitionCN: 指两个不能同时为真的说法；强调逻辑冲突而非不稳定。

entries.definition: A departure from a normal pattern or rule; it stresses deviation rather than self-conflict.
entries.definitionCN: 指偏离正常模式或规则；强调偏离，而非自我冲突。

entries.definition: A measured gap between groups or levels; it is a distance, not a self-contradiction.
entries.definitionCN: 指群体或水平之间可测量的落差；那是一段距离，不是自相矛盾。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations use the real Latin image of standing together, the real prefix of negation and the real data and quality phrases.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想使用真实的拉丁「站在一起」意象、真实的否定前缀，以及真实的数据与质量搭配。

normal.en: con- is together and sistere is stand: consistency is standing together, so in- knocks the pair apart.
normal.cn: con- 是「一起」，sistere 是「站」，consistency 就是站在一起；in- 把这一对打散。

normal.en: If two pages cannot stand side by side without wobbling, you have an inconsistency.
normal.cn: 两页纸若并排站立就摇晃，那就是一处不一致。

normal.en: Data inconsistency, internal inconsistency and glaring inconsistency are three real phrases.
normal.cn: 数据不一致、内部矛盾与明显的前后矛盾是三个真实说法。

normal.en: Count the mismatches and you get the plural: three inconsistencies in one account.
normal.cn: 把对不上的地方数一数就有复数：一份陈述里的三处不符。

normal.en: The word always needs a partner: something is inconsistent with something else.
normal.cn: 这个词总需要一个搭档：某物与另一物不一致。

abstract.en: Consistency is a promise made over time; inconsistency is that promise breaking at the seam.
abstract.cn: 一致性是随时间作出的承诺；不一致就是承诺在接缝处断裂。

abstract.en: A system can be wrong in one place or merely uneven in many; this word covers both kinds of failure.
abstract.cn: 一个系统可能只在一处出错，也可能到处不均匀；这个词覆盖两类失败。

abstract.en: The negative prefix does not mean false, only unsupported: the parts cannot hold each other up.
abstract.cn: 这个否定前缀并不表示「假」，只表示「撑不住」：各部分无法互相支撑。

examples.en: The committee found an inconsistency between the two versions of the contract.
examples.cn: 委员会发现合同的两个版本之间存在不一致。

examples.en: Quality inspectors log every inconsistency they find between batches.
examples.cn: 质检员记录每一处批次之间的不稳定现象。

examples.en: There is a curious inconsistency in the way the two rules are applied.
examples.cn: 两条规则的执行方式存在一处奇怪的不一致。

dict_mnemonic.text: 读作「因肯西斯腾西」——本应站在一起的，偏偏站不齐

root: 来自拉丁语 consistere「站在一起、稳固」← con-「一起」+ sistere「站立」，抽象名词 consistentia 经英语构成 consistency，再加否定前缀 in- 构成 inconsistency。来源链清楚。

sensesIntro.en: Nine senses move from a contradictory sentence through figures and arguments to batches, people, rules, texts, performance and a single mismatched detail.
sensesIntro.cn: 九个义项从一句矛盾的话，经过数字与论证，走到批次、人、规则、文本、表现，最后落到一处具体的不符。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: two pages are made to stand side by side, and one of them keeps tipping over.
core.cn: 核心意象：两页纸被立在一起，其中一页总是倒向一边。

branches.en: THE ARGUMENT: a statement or proof that cannot stand beside itself.
branches.cn: 论证：一句话或一套证明无法与自己并列站稳。

branches.en: THE RECORD: numbers and specific details that refuse to agree.
branches.cn: 记录：数字与具体细节拒绝吻合。

branches.en: THE OUTPUT: batches and performances that rise and fall without a steady line.
branches.cn: 产出：批次与表现忽高忽低，没有稳定的一条线。

branches.en: THE PERSON AND THE RULE: habits that shift and standards applied unevenly.
branches.cn: 人与规则：习惯摇摆，标准适用不均。

branches.en: THE TEXT: a tone that changes without warning and breaks the seam of a book.
branches.cn: 文本：语气无预警地改变，撕开一本书的接缝。

intro.en: Inconsistency layers a negative prefix, a Latin verb for standing, and a noun ending of state.
intro.cn: 这个词叠着一个否定前缀、一个拉丁「站立」动词，以及一个表状态的名词词尾。

latinIntro.en: Latin supplies sistere, consistere and consistentia; the negative prefix in- is added in the English word.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语提供了 sistere、consistere 与 consistentia；否定前缀 in- 是在英语词里加上的。

items.example: It denies the standing together.
items.exampleCN: 它否定了「站在一起」。

items.example: It binds the parts into one stance.
items.exampleCN: 它把各部分绑成一个站姿。

items.exampleCN: 词根画出一个人守住位置的样子。

items.example: Prefix and root form the key verb.
items.exampleCN: 前缀与词根合成关键动词。

items.example: It forms the English noun of state.

items.meaning: to be made up of; to lie in
items.example: The base verb keeps the standing image.
items.exampleCN: 基础动词保留了「站立」意象。

items.example: The adjective describes what holds.
items.exampleCN: 形容词描述站得住的东西。

definition_zh: 拘谨；抑制；克制；抑制作用；抑制因素
definition_en: a force that holds something back, whether an inner reluctance in a person or a process that slows or blocks a reaction, signal or growth
core_image: 一只手伸向门把，却在半空停住，手腕上像被一根看不见的带子拉住
scene: 第一次登台的学生站在幕布后，手心里全是汗，几次想开口都没出声。Stage fright produced a strong inhibition in the young singer.
sceneCN: 这里指人在众人面前放不开的心理拘束（第 1 个义项：心理上的拘谨）；句意为怯场让这位年轻歌手产生了强烈的抑制。图中可辨识物件：幕布、发抖的手、停在半空的麦克风。

pos.zh: 拘谨；抑制；克制；抑制作用

由动词加过去分词词尾构成，义为「拘谨的；受压抑的」
由动词加表示「起……作用的」形容词尾构成，义为「抑制性的」
由动词加表示施动者或物质的名词尾构成，义为「抑制剂」
由否定前缀加过去分词构成，义为「无拘无束的」

senses.title: Inner shyness in company
senses.definition: a strong inner reluctance that makes a person hold back in social situations
senses.definitionCN: 在社交场合中使人退缩的强烈内在阻力
senses.example: Stage fright produced a strong inhibition in the young singer.
senses.exampleCN: 怯场让这位年轻歌手产生了强烈的抑制。
senses.why: The Latin verb meant to hold in; psychology uses it for a brake applied from inside the person.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁动词意为「扣住、收住」；心理学用它指人从内部踩下的刹车。

senses.title: Holding back an impulse
senses.definition: the checking of a desire, impulse or emotion before it becomes action
senses.definitionCN: 在欲望、冲动或情绪变成行动之前将其收住
senses.example: Years of strict training left him with an inhibition about asking for help.
senses.exampleCN: 多年严格训练让他对开口求助有一种克制。
senses.why: What is held in here is not a signal but a wish, and the holding is learned rather than mechanical.
senses.whyCN: 这里被收住的不是信号而是愿望，而且这种收住是学来的，不是机械的。

senses.title: Blocking a chemical reaction
senses.definition: the slowing or blocking of a chemical reaction, often by a substance that acts on an enzyme
senses.definitionCN: 对化学反应减速或阻断，常由作用于酶的物质造成
senses.example: Adding the compound caused inhibition of the enzyme within minutes.
senses.exampleCN: 加入该化合物后，酶在几分钟内受到抑制。
senses.why: Biochemistry kept the image of a hand held back and applied it to molecules that stop a catalyst.
senses.whyCN: 生物化学保留「被拉住的手」这一意象，把它用在对催化剂下手的大分子上。

senses.title: Slowing of growth or division
senses.definition: a reduction in the growth, division or reproduction of cells or organisms
senses.definitionCN: 细胞或生物体在生长、分裂或繁殖上的减弱
senses.example: The extract showed clear inhibition of bacterial growth in the dish.
senses.exampleCN: 该提取物在培养皿中明显抑制了细菌生长。
senses.why: Here the thing held back is a whole population of cells, not one reaction step.
senses.whyCN: 这里被拦住的是整个细胞群体，而不是某一个反应步骤。

senses.title: Quieting of a nerve signal
senses.definition: the dampening of neural activity so that a signal becomes weaker or stops
senses.definitionCN: 神经活动被压弱，使信号变弱或停止
senses.example: The drug produces inhibition of pain signals in the spinal cord.
senses.exampleCN: 这种药物在脊髓中对疼痛信号产生抑制。
senses.why: The nervous system needs brakes as much as accelerators, and the word names those brakes.
senses.whyCN: 神经系统既需要加速器也需要刹车，这个词就指那些刹车。

senses.title: Suppression of a bodily function
senses.definition: the reduction or stopping of a secretion, reflex or organ function
senses.definitionCN: 对分泌、反射或器官功能的减弱或中止
senses.example: The treatment led to inhibition of acid secretion in the stomach.
senses.exampleCN: 该治疗导致胃酸分泌受到抑制。
senses.why: Medicine applies the same noun to any function that is made to quiet down.
senses.whyCN: 医学把同一个名词用于任何被压下去的功能。

senses.title: A social taboo or constraint
senses.definition: a rule or custom that keeps people from saying or doing something
senses.definitionCN: 使人不敢说或不敢做的规则与习俗
senses.example: The old inhibition against discussing money has weakened among younger buyers.
senses.exampleCN: 年轻消费者中，不谈钱的老禁忌已经减弱。
senses.why: The brake is no longer inside one mind but shared by a community.
senses.whyCN: 这时刹车不在某个人心里，而为一个群体所共有。

senses.title: Stiffness in performance
senses.definition: a lack of ease that makes a performance look guarded or forced
senses.definitionCN: 使表演显得拘束或做作的不自然状态
senses.example: The director asked the actors to drop their inhibition and move more freely.
senses.exampleCN: 导演要求演员放下拘束，动作更自由些。
senses.why: On stage the inner brake becomes visible: the body moves as if a strap were still on it.
senses.whyCN: 在舞台上，内心的刹车变得可见：身体动起来像还拴着带子。

intro.en: Inhibition comes from a Latin verb meaning to hold in, built from a prefix of inwardness and a root meaning to have or hold; psychology and biochemistry later gave it two technical lives.
intro.cn: 这个词来自拉丁语表示「扣在里面」的动词，由表示「向内」的前缀与表示「持有、握住」的词根构成；心理学与生物化学后来给了它两条技术生命。

items.en: habere meant to have, to hold, to keep in one's hand.
items.cn: habere 意为「有、握住、拿在手里」。

items.en: in- carried the sense of in or against, so inhibere was to hold in, check or restrain.
items.cn: in- 带有「在内、对着」的意思，因此 inhibere 意为「扣住、制止、约束」。

items.en: The past participle named something already held back, and it became the stem of the English family.
items.cn: 过去分词指已被收住的东西，后来成为英语这一族词的词干。

items.en: The action noun inhibitio named the act of holding in or checking.
items.cn: 动作名词 inhibitio 命名「收住、制止」这一行为。

items.en: English first used the word for restraining a legal or physical action; the exact first date is not certain, but the Latin line is clear.
items.cn: 英语最初用它指对法律行为或身体动作的制止；具体首见年份不确定，但拉丁来源线索清楚。

items.en: In the twentieth century the word split into an inner brake of the mind and a chemical brake on enzymes and growth.
items.cn: 二十世纪这个词分成两支：心智内部的刹车，以及作用于酶与生长的化学刹车。

note.en: The first group shares root or shape with inhibition; the second group names nearby brakes, and the note keeps their mechanisms apart.
note.cn: 第一组在词根或形音上与 inhibition 相近；第二组是邻近的「刹车」类词，说明中把它们的机制分开。

entries.definition: The verb meaning to hold back, slow or forbid a process or behaviour.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「抑制、阻碍、使拘束」。

entries.definition: Describing a person who is held back and shows it in behaviour.
entries.definitionCN: 形容一个人受拘束，并在行为上表现出来。

entries.definition: A technical adjective for a signal, drug or cell that suppresses activity.
entries.definitionCN: 技术形容词，指压抑活动的信号、药物或细胞。

entries.definition: A substance or agent that slows a reaction or a biological process.
entries.definitionCN: 指减缓反应或生物过程的物质或因子。

entries.definition: A public display; it uses the same holding root with ex-, to hold out, so the direction is opposite.
entries.definitionCN: 指公开展览；同一「握住」词根配上表示「向外」的前缀，方向正好相反。

entries.definition: The act of living in a place; it looks close but comes from a verb for dwelling, not for holding in.
entries.definitionCN: 指居住在某地；形近，但来自表示「居住」的动词，而非「扣住」。

entries.definition: Self-control or an external limit that keeps action in check; broader and often deliberate.
entries.definitionCN: 指自我控制或外部限制，使行动受约束；更宽泛，且常是主动的。

entries.definition: Forceful putting down of a feeling, fact or activity; it stresses power and often concealment.
entries.definitionCN: 指对情绪、事实或活动的强力压下；强调权力，常含隐瞒。

entries.definition: An outside signal or action that disrupts a process rather than holding it from within.
entries.definitionCN: 指从外部扰乱过程的信号或行为，而非从内部拉住它。

entries.definition: A thing standing in the way that must be removed or gone round; it blocks movement, not a function.
entries.definitionCN: 指挡在路上、需要清除或绕开的东西；它阻碍的是移动，不是功能。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations use the real Latin hold-in image, the real psychology and biochemistry pairs, and the real sister words.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想使用真实的拉丁「扣住」意象、真实的心理学与生物化学搭配，以及真实的同族词。

normal.en: in- plus habere, to hold: inhibition is something held in, and the hand stops halfway.
normal.cn: in- 加 habere「握住」：抑制就是被扣在里面的东西，手停在半途。

normal.en: A car needs both an engine and a brake; a mind and a cell need inhibition too.
normal.cn: 汽车既需要引擎也需要刹车；心智与细胞同样需要抑制。

normal.en: Social inhibition, enzyme inhibition and growth inhibition are three real phrases.
normal.cn: 社交拘谨、酶抑制与生长抑制是三个真实搭配。

normal.en: Remove the brake and you get the negative adjective: uninhibited, without restraint.
normal.cn: 把刹车拆掉就得到否定形容词 uninhibited，即无拘无束。

normal.en: The same noun covers a shy singer and a stopped enzyme because both are held back.
normal.cn: 同一个名词既指害羞的歌手又指被抑制的酶，因为两者都是被拉住的。

abstract.en: A brake is not a flaw in the machine; without it, every impulse becomes movement.
abstract.cn: 刹车不是机器的缺陷；没有它，每个冲动都会变成动作。

abstract.en: Inhibition is pressure applied at a distance, felt as a hand that never quite arrives.
abstract.cn: 抑制是隔着距离施加的压力，感觉像一只始终到不了的手。

abstract.en: The word hides its own paradox: what holds you back also makes steady action possible.
abstract.cn: 这个词藏着悖论：拉住你的东西，也让稳定的行动成为可能。

examples.en: Her inhibition faded once the audience began to laugh with her.
examples.cn: 观众和她一起笑起来之后，她的拘束就消散了。

examples.en: The assay measures inhibition of the enzyme at several concentrations.
examples.cn: 该检测在多个浓度下测量酶的抑制程度。

examples.en: Cultural inhibition around silence made the meeting unusually slow.
examples.cn: 围绕沉默的文化禁忌让会议异常拖沓。

dict_mnemonic.text: 读作「因希比申」——把手往回收，就是抑制

root: 来自拉丁语 inhibere「扣住、制止」← in-「在内、对着」+ habere「握住、持有」，过去分词 inhibitus，动作名词 inhibitio；经法语进入英语。来源链清楚，首见年代为约数。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses run from social shyness and held-back impulses to chemical, cellular, neural and medical brakes, then to taboo and stage stiffness.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项从社交拘谨与收住的冲动，走到化学、细胞、神经与医学上的刹车，再到禁忌与舞台上的拘束。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a hand reaches for a door and stops in mid-air, held by an unseen strap.
core.cn: 核心意象：一只手伸向门把，却在半空停住，被一根看不见的带子拉住。

branches.en: THE MIND'S BRAKE: shyness in company and a wish checked before it acts.
branches.cn: 心智的刹车：人前的拘谨，以及行动前被收住的愿望。

branches.en: THE CHEMISTRY AND THE CLINIC: reactions and secretions slowed by a substance.
branches.cn: 化学与临床：反应与分泌被某种物质减慢。

branches.en: THE CELL AND THE NERVE: growth and pain signals quieted from inside the body.
branches.cn: 细胞与神经：生长与疼痛信号在体内被压下去。

branches.en: THE SHARED TABOO: a rule that keeps a whole community from speaking.
branches.cn: 共享的禁忌：让整个群体缄口的一条规则。

branches.en: THE STRAP ON STAGE: a body that moves as if still held.
branches.cn: 舞台上的带子：身体动起来像仍被拉住。

intro.en: Inhibition is a Latin verb with an inward prefix, a holding root and an action-noun ending.
intro.cn: 这个词是一个拉丁动词加上内向前缀、握住词根与动作名词词尾。

latinIntro.en: Latin supplies habere, inhibere and inhibitio; the English family keeps the same holding image in every member.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语提供了 habere、inhibere 与 inhibitio；英语这一族的每个成员都保留同一个「握住」意象。

items.exampleCN: 它把「握」变成「扣住」。

items.example: The root is the hand that keeps the object.
items.exampleCN: 这个词根就是握着对象的那只手。

items.example: Prefix and root form the key verb.
items.exampleCN: 前缀与词根合成关键动词。

items.example: The participle supplies the adjective stem.
items.exampleCN: 分词提供了形容词词干。

items.example: It forms the action noun.
items.exampleCN: 它构成动作名词。

items.example: The base English verb keeps the brake.
items.exampleCN: 英语基础动词保留了刹车。

items.example: It forms inhibited, held back in behaviour.
items.exampleCN: 它构成 inhibited，指行为上受拘束。

items.example: It forms inhibitory, the technical adjective.
items.exampleCN: 它构成技术形容词 inhibitory。

items.example: It forms inhibitor, the substance that brakes.
items.exampleCN: 它构成 inhibitor，指踩刹车的物质。

items.example: It forms uninhibited, the brake released.
items.exampleCN: 它构成 uninhibited，即刹车被放开。

definition_zh: 干扰；干涉；妨碍；干预；干涉现象
definition_en: the act of entering or crossing something that is already in progress, whether a signal, a game, a legal right or another person's affairs
core_image: 两束水波在池中相撞，波峰与波谷叠成高低不一的纹路，一旁的仪器屏幕跳出杂波
scene: 两台路由器放在同一间小屋里，电视画面开始出现雪花，工程师拿着频谱仪在窗边来回走动。Thick walls reduced the interference between the two signals.
sceneCN: 这里指两个信号互相搅扰（第 2 个义项：信号与电波干扰）；句意为厚墙减轻了两个信号之间的干扰。图中可辨识物件：两台路由器、雪花画面、频谱仪、窗边的工程师。

pos.zh: 干扰；干涉；妨碍；干涉现象

由动词加现在分词词尾构成，义为「爱管闲事的；干扰的」
由动词加表示施动者的名词尾构成，义为「干扰源；干涉者」
