senses.title: Unwanted involvement in another's affairs
senses.titleCN: 对他人事务的不当插手
senses.definition: the act of stepping into a matter that belongs to someone else and altering its course
senses.definitionCN: 介入属于他人的事情并改变其进程
senses.example: The minister denied any interference in the selection process.
senses.exampleCN: 部长否认对遴选过程有任何干预。
senses.why: The old verb meant to strike between two parties; the noun keeps the sense of a third force entering a pair.
senses.whyCN: 古动词意为「在两者之间击打」；名词保留了「第三方力量插入一对关系」的意思。

senses.title: Crossing of an electromagnetic signal
senses.titleCN: 电波与信号的互相搅扰
senses.definition: unwanted energy or a second transmission that disturbs a signal being received
senses.definitionCN: 不需要的能量或第二路传输扰乱了正在接收的信号
senses.example: Thick walls reduced the interference between the two signals.
senses.exampleCN: 厚墙减轻了两个信号之间的干扰。
senses.why: Radio engineering gave the word its most familiar modern body: one wave strikes across another.
senses.whyCN: 无线电工程给了这个词最熟悉的现代实体：一道波横击另一道波。

senses.title: Noise that spoils sound or data
senses.titleCN: 破坏声音或数据的噪声
senses.definition: noise or cross-talk that makes audio, video or data less clear
senses.definitionCN: 使音频、视频或数据变得不清楚的噪声或串扰
senses.example: Background interference made the recording unusable.
senses.exampleCN: 背景干扰让这段录音无法使用。
senses.why: The signal need not be another message; random noise also crosses the channel.
senses.whyCN: 干扰不一定来自另一条消息；随机噪声同样会横穿信道。

senses.title: Blocking or distracting a player
senses.definition: an illegal or unsporting act that obstructs or distracts an opposing player
senses.definitionCN: 阻挡或分散对方球员的违规或不正当行为
senses.example: The referee called interference on the play.
senses.exampleCN: 裁判在这次进攻中判了干扰犯规。
senses.why: Sport applies the word to a body put in the way of another body.
senses.whyCN: 体育把这个词用于一具身体挡在另一具身体前面。

senses.title: Legal meddling with a right or contract
senses.definition: wrongful action that disrupts a contract, property right or legal process
senses.definitionCN: 不法行为破坏合同、财产权或法律程序
senses.example: The supplier sued the rival firm for interference with its contract.
senses.exampleCN: 供应商起诉竞争对手妨碍其合同。
senses.why: Law turns the crossing into a claim: a third party has reached into a relationship it did not own.
senses.whyCN: 法律把这次横插变成一项诉求：第三方伸进了它并不拥有的关系。

senses.title: Disruption of memory or learning
senses.definition: the weakening of recall or learning when similar material competes or overlaps
senses.definitionCN: 相似材料竞争或重叠时，回忆与学习被削弱
senses.example: New vocabulary caused interference with the words learned the day before.
senses.exampleCN: 新词汇对前一天学的词造成了干扰。
senses.why: Psychology found that one memory can strike across another and blur it.
senses.whyCN: 心理学发现一段记忆可以横击另一段，把它弄模糊。

senses.title: Combining of waves in physics
senses.definition: the superposition of two or more waves, producing reinforcement or cancellation
senses.definitionCN: 两列或多列波叠加，产生增强或抵消
senses.example: The lab demonstrated interference using two slits and a laser.
senses.exampleCN: 实验室用双缝和激光演示了干涉。
senses.why: This technical sense is neutral, even beautiful: crossing waves need not spoil anything.
senses.whyCN: 这个技术义是中性的，甚至很美：波的交汇未必破坏什么。

senses.title: Unwanted electrical disturbance in a device
senses.definition: stray voltage or current that upsets the normal operation of equipment
senses.definitionCN: 使设备无法正常工作的杂散电压或电流
senses.example: The motor produced interference that tripped the sensor.
senses.exampleCN: 电机产生的干扰让传感器跳闸。
senses.why: The abstract crossing becomes a concrete fault inside a circuit.
senses.whyCN: 抽象的「横插」变成电路内部一处具体的故障。

senses.title: An unnecessary intervention
senses.definition: action taken by an outsider that was neither asked for nor needed
senses.definitionCN: 外部人员采取的既未被请求也非必要的行为
senses.example: Her parents' interference made the negotiation harder.
senses.exampleCN: 她父母的介入让谈判更难进行。
senses.why: The word judges the entry, not just describes it: the outsider was not invited.
senses.whyCN: 这个词不只描述进入，还对它作出评判：外人并未受邀。

intro.en: Interference grew from a French verb meaning to strike between two parties, with a disputed Latin alternative; radio and physics then made the crossing literal.
intro.cn: 这个词源自法语表示「在两者之间击打」的动词，另有一条有争议的拉丁构成说；无线电与物理学后来让「横穿」变得具体。

items.en: ferire meant to strike, to hit; the root is clear and survives in many Latin compounds.
items.cn: ferire 意为「击打、撞击」；这个词根清楚，并在许多拉丁复合词中留存。

items.en: entre- meant between, so s'entreferir described two parties striking each other.
items.cn: entre- 表示「在……之间」，因此 s'entreferir 描述双方互相击打。

items.en: Some dictionaries derive the English word from the French verb, while others point to a Latin inter- plus ferire pattern; because the two routes compete, the exact formation is source uncertain.
items.cn: 一些词典认为英语词来自法语动词，另一些则指向拉丁语 inter- 加 ferire 的构成；两条路线并存，因此确切构词来源不确定。

items.en: English adopted the verb in the seventeenth century in the sense of meddling, and the noun followed.
items.cn: 英语在十七世纪借入这个动词，意为「插手」，名词随后出现。

items.en: In the early twentieth century the word attached itself to waves that disturb one another.
items.cn: 二十世纪初，这个词开始依附于互相扰乱的电波。

items.en: Optics made interference a neutral superposition, while law made it a wrongful crossing of rights.
items.cn: 光学让「干涉」成为中性的叠加，法律则让它成为对权利的违法侵入。

note.en: The first group shares the inter- prefix or the root; the second group names nearby kinds of disruption and keeps their mechanisms apart.
note.cn: 第一组共享 inter- 前缀或同一词根；第二组是邻近的扰乱类说法，说明中把各自机制分开。

entries.definition: The verb to meddle, obstruct or disturb a process.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「干涉、妨碍、干扰」。

entries.definition: The adjective for someone who meddles, or for a signal that disturbs.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，指爱插手的，或指造成干扰的。

entries.definition: An instrument that measures wave interference with great precision.
entries.definitionCN: 指利用波的干涉进行精密测量的仪器。

entries.definition: A body substance named for interfering with viral replication.
entries.definitionCN: 指因干扰病毒复制而得名的一种体内物质。

entries.definition: A gap in time or space; it shares the prefix but its root is a rampart word, not a striking word.
entries.definitionCN: 指时间或空间上的间隔；共享前缀，但词根是「壁垒」而非「击打」。

entries.definition: The act of stepping in to change an outcome; it shares the prefix but not the striking root.
entries.definitionCN: 指介入以改变结果；共享前缀，但没有「击打」词根。

entries.definition: A thing that stands in the way of movement or progress and must be removed or avoided.
entries.definitionCN: 指挡在移动或前进路上的东西，需要清除或绕开。

entries.definition: A brake applied from inside a person, cell or process, not a force crossing in from outside.
entries.definitionCN: 指从人、细胞或过程内部施加的刹车，而非从外部横插的力量。

entries.definition: A breaking of the normal flow of an activity; it stresses the interruption, not the crossing.
entries.definitionCN: 指活动正常流程被打断；强调中断，而非横穿。

entries.definition: A noisy or forceful upset of a quiet state or system.
entries.definitionCN: 指对安静状态或系统的喧闹或强力搅扰。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations use the real between-and-strike image, the real radio and physics phrases, and the real legal sense.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想使用真实的「在两者之间击打」意象、真实的无线电与物理搭配，以及真实的法律含义。

normal.en: entre meant between and ferir meant strike: interference is a third hand hitting a pair.
normal.cn: entre 是「之间」，ferir 是「击打」：干扰就是第三只手打在一对关系上。

normal.en: Two waves cross and make a striped pattern on the wall, which is literal interference.
normal.cn: 两道波交汇，在墙上留下条纹，这就是字面意义上的干涉。

normal.en: Electromagnetic interference, radio interference and interference pattern are three real phrases.
normal.cn: 电磁干扰、无线电干扰与干涉图样是三个真实搭配。

normal.en: A referee calls interference when a body is put where it does not belong.
normal.cn: 当一具身体出现在不该出现的位置，裁判就判干扰。

normal.en: Interference with a contract is the legal name for reaching into someone else's deal.
normal.cn: 妨碍合同是「伸手进入别人的交易」的法律名称。

abstract.en: Two truths can overlap and either reinforce or cancel, just as two waves do.
abstract.cn: 两个真相可以重叠，或增强或抵消，正如两道波。

abstract.en: Interference is not always damage: in physics the crossing is the whole point of the experiment.
abstract.cn: 干扰并不总是损害：在物理学里，交汇正是实验的全部意义。

abstract.en: Every unwanted entry assumes a boundary; the word quietly tells you where the line was.
abstract.cn: 每一次不受欢迎的进入都预设了一条边界；这个词悄悄告诉你界线在哪里。

examples.en: The airline blamed interference from a nearby transmitter for the lost signal.
examples.cn: 航空公司把信号丢失归咎于附近发射机的干扰。

examples.en: Wave interference explains both the bright bands and the dark ones.
examples.cn: 波的干涉既能解释亮纹，也能解释暗纹。

examples.en: The court found interference with a valid employment contract.
examples.cn: 法院认定存在对一份有效雇佣合同的妨碍。

dict_mnemonic.text: 读作「因特菲润斯」——插到两者中间去击打，就是干扰

root: 源自古法语 s'entreferir「互相击打」← entre-「在……之间」+ ferir「击打」← 拉丁语 ferire「击打」。另有学者认为直接来自拉丁语 inter- 加 ferire，两种构成路线并存，确切构词来源不确定；英语十七世纪借入动词，名词随后出现。

sensesIntro.en: Nine senses move from meddling in affairs and crossing signals through sport, law, memory, wave physics and circuits to an unwanted intervention.
sensesIntro.cn: 九个义项从插手他人事务、信号互扰，经过体育、法律、记忆、波的物理与电路，最后落到不受欢迎的介入。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: two water waves meet in a pool and leave a striped shadow on the wall.
core.cn: 核心意象：两道水波在池中相遇，在墙上投下条纹状的影子。

branches.en: THE AFFAIRS: an uninvited third hand enters a pair.
branches.cn: 事务：一只未被邀请的第三只手插入一对关系。

branches.en: THE SIGNAL AND THE CIRCUIT: waves, noise and stray current cross a channel.
branches.cn: 信号与电路：电波、噪声与杂散电流横穿信道。

branches.en: THE PLAY: a body placed where another body needs to go.
branches.cn: 比赛：一具身体挡在另一具身体要去的地方。

branches.en: THE RIGHT: a legal claim crossed by an outsider.
branches.cn: 权利：一项法律诉求被外人横插。

branches.en: THE MIND AND THE LAB: memories blurred by overlap, waves combined on purpose.
branches.cn: 心智与实验室：记忆因重叠而模糊，波被有意叠加。

intro.en: Interference is built on a prefix meaning between and a Latin root meaning to strike, with an action-noun ending.
intro.cn: 这个词建立在一个表示「之间」的前缀、一个表示「击打」的拉丁词根和一个动作名词词尾上。

latinIntro.en: Latin clearly supplies ferire; the prefix may come through French or directly from Latin, so the assembly line is partly uncertain.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语明确提供了 ferire；前缀可能经法语而来，也可能直接取自拉丁语，因此拼装路线有部分不确定。

items.example: It places the action between two parties.
items.exampleCN: 它把动作放在两者之间。

items.example: The root keeps the physical blow.
items.exampleCN: 词根保留了物理上的一击。

items.example: The French route carries the same prefix.
items.exampleCN: 法语路线带着同样的前缀。

items.example: It is the French form of the Latin root.
items.exampleCN: 它是拉丁词根的法语形式。

items.example: The base verb names the crossing.
items.exampleCN: 基础动词命名这次横插。

items.example: It forms the English noun.
items.exampleCN: 它构成英语名词。

items.example: It forms interfering, the meddling adjective.
items.exampleCN: 它构成 interfering，指爱插手的。

items.example: It forms interferer, a source of disturbance.
items.exampleCN: 它构成 interferer，指干扰源。

items.example: It forms interferometer, the wave-measuring tool.
items.exampleCN: 它构成 interferometer，即测量波的仪器。

items.example: It forms interferon, named for interference.
items.exampleCN: 它构成 interferon，因「干扰」得名。

derivatives.zh: 同词干动词，义为「干涉；干扰」
由现在分词构成，义为「爱插手的」
由施动者词尾构成，义为「干扰源」
由测量仪器词尾构成，义为「干涉仪」
由生物物质词尾构成，义为「干扰素」

definition_zh: 障碍物；阻碍；障碍；绊脚石；壁垒
definition_en: something that stands in the way and must be removed, crossed or gone around before progress can continue
core_image: 一条小径正中横着一块大石，行人提着包从旁边的窄缝侧身挤过
scene: 山道正中倒着一棵大树，骑车的人只好下车，抬着车从路旁的草坡绕过去。A fallen tree became an obstacle on the mountain road.
sceneCN: 这里指挡在路上的实物（第 1 个义项：物理障碍物）；句意为倒下的树成了山道上的障碍。图中可辨识物件：横倒的树干、单车、草坡、被堵住的路面。

derivatives.zh: 由本词加表示路线的名词构成的复合说法，义为「障碍赛道」；本词没有常见的派生词族
由本词加表示比赛的名词构成的复合说法，义为「障碍赛」
本词的复数形式，义为「多处障碍」

senses.title: A physical thing blocking the way
senses.definition: an object that physically prevents passage along a route
senses.definitionCN: 物理上阻止人沿路线通行的物体
senses.example: A fallen tree became an obstacle on the mountain road.
senses.exampleCN: 倒下的树成了山道上的障碍。
senses.why: The Latin verb meant to stand against; the noun first names a thing that literally stands in front of you.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁动词意为「站在对面」；这个名词最初指一件字面意义上立在你面前的东西。

senses.title: A hindrance to progress
senses.definition: a condition, rule or shortage that slows or prevents an intended outcome
senses.definitionCN: 减缓或阻止预期结果的条件、规则或短缺
senses.example: Lack of funding is the main obstacle to the research.
senses.exampleCN: 资金不足是这项研究的主要障碍。
senses.why: Once the thing standing in the way is no longer physical, the word keeps the same geometry: something is in front of the goal.
senses.whyCN: 当挡路之物不再有形，这个词仍保留同样的几何关系：有东西横在目标前面。

senses.title: A hurdle in sport
senses.titleCN: 体育比赛中的栏架与障碍
senses.definition: a fence, hurdle or water jump that a competitor must clear
senses.definitionCN: 选手必须越过的栏架、栅栏或水沟
senses.example: She cleared every obstacle in the final lap.
senses.exampleCN: 她在最后一圈越过了每一个障碍。
senses.why: Sport turns the blocking object into a designed test that must be jumped rather than removed.
senses.whyCN: 体育把挡路的物体变成设计好的考验：必须跳过，而不是搬走。

senses.title: A defensive barrier in warfare
senses.definition: a barricade, wire or ditch built to slow an advancing force
senses.definitionCN: 为迟滞对方推进而设置的路障、铁丝网或壕沟
senses.example: Engineers laid an obstacle belt before the position.
senses.exampleCN: 工兵在阵地前布设了一条障碍带。
senses.why: Here the obstacle is deliberately placed by the defender, so blocking becomes a tactic.
senses.whyCN: 这里的障碍由防守方故意设置，阻挡因此成为一种战术。

senses.title: A barrier to communication
senses.definition: a difference of language, culture or channel that keeps a message from arriving
senses.definitionCN: 语言、文化或渠道差异使信息无法抵达
senses.example: Poor translation created an obstacle between the two delegations.
senses.exampleCN: 糟糕的翻译在两个代表团之间造成了障碍。
senses.why: The thing in the way is now a gap in understanding rather than a stone.
senses.whyCN: 此时挡路的不再是石头，而是理解上的缺口。

senses.title: A mental barrier
senses.definition: an inner fear or belief that stops a person from acting
senses.definitionCN: 阻止人行动的内在恐惧或信念
senses.example: Fear of failure was the real obstacle, not the exam.
senses.exampleCN: 真正的障碍是对失败的恐惧，而不是考试。
senses.why: The stone moves inside the mind; the word follows it there.
senses.whyCN: 石头移进了心里；这个词也跟着去了那里。

senses.title: An economic or trade barrier
senses.definition: a tariff, quota or regulation that restricts the movement of goods
senses.definitionCN: 限制商品流动的关税、配额或法规
senses.example: The new tariff became an obstacle to exports.
senses.exampleCN: 新关税成了出口的障碍。
senses.why: Policy builds invisible walls, and the old stone word still fits them.
senses.whyCN: 政策筑起看不见的墙，这个古老的石头词依然适用。

senses.title: The sticking point in a negotiation
senses.definition: the one issue on which talks cannot move forward
senses.definitionCN: 使谈判无法推进的那一个议题
senses.example: Payment terms remained the chief obstacle to the deal.
senses.exampleCN: 付款条件仍是这笔交易的主要症结。
senses.why: In a room of words, one unresolved point can stand in the road like a boulder.
senses.whyCN: 在一屋子言辞里，一个未解决的议题也能像巨石一样横在路上。

senses.title: An object a machine must avoid
senses.titleCN: 机器必须避开的障碍物
senses.definition: an object detected by a vehicle or robot that must be routed around
senses.definitionCN: 车辆或机器人检测到、必须绕开的物体
senses.example: The robot stopped when its sensor detected an obstacle.
senses.exampleCN: 传感器检测到障碍物时，机器人停了下来。
senses.why: Robotics borrowed the plain physical sense and gave it a detection routine.
senses.whyCN: 机器人学借用了最朴素的物理义，并给它配上一套检测程序。

intro.en: Obstacle is a Latin verb for standing against, turned into a noun for the thing that stands in the way; English took it through French.
intro.cn: 这个词来自拉丁语表示「站在对面」的动词，转为指「挡在路上的东西」的名词；英语经法语借入。

items.en: stare meant to stand, to remain in place; it is the root of a large family of standing words.
items.cn: stare 意为「站立、留在原地」，是一大类「站立」词的词根。

items.en: ob- meant against, in front of, or towards, and it fixes the direction of the standing.
items.cn: ob- 意为「对着、在前面、朝向」，它规定了「站」的方向。

items.en: obstare was to stand in front of a person or thing, hence to hinder.
items.cn: obstare 意为「站在某人或某物前面」，因此引申为「阻碍」。

items.en: The noun obstaculum named the thing that stands in the way, not the act of standing.
items.cn: 名词 obstaculum 指挡在路上的那个东西，而不是「站」这个动作。

items.en: Old French obstacle carried the noun into English in the fourteenth century; the first date is approximate but the line is clear.
items.cn: 古法语 obstacle 在十四世纪把这个名词带进英语；首见年份为约数，但来源线索清楚。

items.en: Sport, trade, psychology and robotics each reused the stone-in-the-road image for a barrier of their own kind.
items.cn: 体育、贸易、心理学与机器人学各自把「路上的石头」这一意象用于本领域的壁垒。

note.en: The first group shares the standing root or looks close; the second group names nearby barriers and distinguishes how each one blocks.
note.cn: 第一组共享「站立」词根或形音相近；第二组是邻近的阻碍类词，说明中区分各自的阻挡方式。

entries.definition: Stubbornly refusing to change; it uses the same standing-against root for a person's will.
entries.definitionCN: 指固执地拒绝改变；用同一「站着对抗」词根来描述人的意志。

entries.definition: The medical field of childbirth; its Latin source named a midwife as one who stands before the mother.
entries.definitionCN: 指产科医学；其拉丁来源把助产士称为「站在母亲前面的人」。

entries.definition: To block or get in the way; it looks related but is built on a root meaning to pile up, not to stand.
entries.definitionCN: 指阻塞或挡路；形近，但其词根意为「堆起」，而非「站立」。

entries.definition: Several things standing in the way at once.
entries.definitionCN: 指同时挡在路上的多件东西。

entries.definition: A structure or rule that keeps things apart; it separates rather than merely blocking a route.
entries.definitionCN: 指把事物隔开的结构或规则；它重在分隔，而不只是挡住路线。

entries.definition: A small barrier to jump over, or a difficulty to pass; it suggests a sequence of tests.
entries.definitionCN: 指需跳过的矮栏，或需通过的难关；暗示一连串考验。

entries.definition: Something that slows progress, often a defect or burden carried along.
entries.definitionCN: 指拖慢进展的东西，常是随身带着的缺陷或负担。

entries.definition: An outside force crossing into a process and disturbing it; it acts on the process, not on the road.
entries.definitionCN: 指外部力量横插进一个过程并加以扰乱；它作用于过程，而非挡在路上。

entries.definition: A brake applied from inside a person or system; it restrains rather than stands in front.
entries.definitionCN: 指从人或系统内部施加的刹车；它重在拉住，而非立在前面。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations use the real Latin stand-against image, the real sport and trade phrases, and the real sister roots.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想使用真实的拉丁「站着对抗」意象、真实的体育与贸易搭配，以及真实的同根词。

normal.en: ob- is against and stare is stand: an obstacle is something standing against your path.
normal.cn: ob- 是对着，stare 是站立：障碍就是立在路对面挡住你的东西。

normal.en: The word is a noun for the stone, not for the walking; remove the object and the road reopens.
normal.cn: 这个词是那块石头的名词，不是走路的名词；搬走物体，路就重新打开。

normal.en: Obstacle course and obstacle race are two real sporting phrases.
normal.cn: 障碍赛道与障碍赛是两个真实的体育说法。

normal.en: A trade tariff is an invisible obstacle, but the geometry is the same.
normal.cn: 贸易关税是一道看不见的障碍，但几何关系完全相同。

normal.en: A robot detects an obstacle and routes around it, which is the plain sense in a machine.
normal.cn: 机器人检测到障碍物并绕行，这就是这个词在机器里的朴素用法。

abstract.en: An obstacle is defined by the direction you want to go; the same stone is scenery to a walker heading elsewhere.
abstract.cn: 障碍是由你想去的方向定义的；同一块石头，对朝别处走的行人只是风景。

abstract.en: Some obstacles are placed on purpose, and some are only feared; both stop the feet.
abstract.cn: 有些障碍是故意设置的，有些只存在于恐惧中；两者都能让脚停住。

abstract.en: The word is not an enemy but a test of route: every path proves itself by what it goes around.
abstract.cn: 这个词不是敌人，而是对路线的检验：每条路都用它绕开的东西证明自己。

examples.en: The fallen bridge was the last obstacle between the village and the hospital.
examples.cn: 断桥是村庄与医院之间的最后一道障碍。

examples.en: High interest rates remain an obstacle to small businesses.
examples.cn: 高利率仍是小企业的障碍。

examples.en: The negotiators cleared the main obstacle with a single compromise.
examples.cn: 谈判者用一次妥协清除了主要症结。

dict_mnemonic.text: 读作「奥布斯脱克」——有东西「站在对面」挡着路

root: 来自拉丁语 obstaculum「阻碍物」← obstare「站在前面阻挡」← ob-「对着、在前」+ stare「站立」；经古法语 obstacle 于十四世纪进入英语。词源链清楚，首见年代为约数。

sensesIntro.en: Nine senses run from a stone in the road through abstract hindrance, sport, warfare, language, mind, trade and negotiation to a robot's detected object.
sensesIntro.cn: 九个义项从路上的一块石头，经过抽象阻碍、体育、战争、语言、心智、贸易与谈判，最后落到机器人检测到的物体。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a boulder sits across a narrow path, and every walker must squeeze past its edge.
core.cn: 核心意象：一块巨石横在窄路上，每个行人都要从它边缘挤过去。

branches.en: THE STONE AND THE WIRE: a physical object, whether natural or built for defence.
branches.cn: 石头与铁丝：自然存在的实物，或为防御而设的实物。

branches.en: THE RULE AND THE TARIFF: an abstract condition or a policy wall in the way.
branches.cn: 规则与关税：抽象条件或政策之墙挡在路上。

branches.en: THE HURDLE AND THE SENSOR: an obstacle designed for sport or detected by a machine.
branches.cn: 栏架与传感器：为体育设计的障碍，或被机器检测到的障碍。

branches.en: THE WORD AND THE FEAR: a gap in understanding or a belief that stops the feet.
branches.cn: 话语与恐惧：理解上的缺口，或阻止脚步的信念。

branches.en: THE STICKING POINT: one unresolved issue that holds a whole deal in place.
branches.cn: 症结：一个未解决的议题把整笔交易卡住。

intro.en: Obstacle is a prepositional prefix plus a verb of standing plus a noun ending for a thing.
intro.cn: 这个词是一个方位前缀、一个「站立」动词，再加一个表「物」的名词词尾。

latinIntro.en: Latin supplies stare, obstare and obstaculum; the English noun came through Old French with the same pieces.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语提供了 stare、obstare 与 obstaculum；英语名词经古法语而来，构件相同。

items.example: It fixes the direction of the standing.
items.exampleCN: 它规定「站」的方向。

items.example: The root names a body in place.
items.exampleCN: 词根命名一个立在原地的身体。

items.example: Prefix and root form the key verb.
items.exampleCN: 前缀与词根合成关键动词。

items.example: The noun names the thing, not the act.
items.exampleCN: 名词指物，不指动作。

items.example: It turns the verb into a concrete noun.
items.exampleCN: 它把动词变成具体名词。

items.example: The borrowed noun keeps the stone image.
items.exampleCN: 借入的名词保留石头意象。

items.example: The compound adds a designed route.
items.exampleCN: 复合词加上一条设计好的路线。

items.example: The compound adds competition.
items.exampleCN: 复合词加上竞赛。

items.example: A sister word applies the root to the will.
items.exampleCN: 同根词把这个词根用于意志。

derivatives.zh: 由本词加路线名词构成的复合说法，义为「障碍赛道」
由本词加比赛名词构成的复合说法，义为「障碍赛」
本词复数，义为「多处障碍」

definition_zh: 前所未有的；史无前例的；空前的；无先例可循的
definition_en: never having happened, existed or been done before, so that no earlier case exists to serve as a guide
core_image: 档案柜里一排旧水位刻线都很低，今年的水痕却高过所有旧线，旁边的人仰头看着新刻痕
scene: 气象站的老档案里，过去一百年的最高水位都低于今年的刻线，工作人员围着新水痕拍照。The flood reached an unprecedented level last week.
sceneCN: 这里指水位达到从未有过的高度（第 1 个义项：规模或程度前所未有）；句意为上周洪水达到了前所未有的水位。图中可辨识物件：旧档案柜、一排低刻线、高过所有旧线的新水痕、拍照的工作人员。

pos.zh: 前所未有的；史无前例的；空前的

derivatives.zh: 由前缀加「行走」词根构成的名词，义为「先例；在前的」
同一词根的基础动词，义为「先于；走在前面」
由动词加现在分词词尾构成，义为「在前的」
由词干加表示次序的名词词尾构成，义为「优先；优先权」
由本词加副词词尾构成，义为「前所未有地」

senses.title: A scale never reached before
senses.definition: existing at a size or intensity for which no earlier example can be found
senses.definitionCN: 达到一个找不到先前例子的规模或强度
senses.example: The flood reached an unprecedented level last week.
senses.exampleCN: 上周洪水达到了前所未有的水位。
senses.why: The negative prefix removes the earlier case, and the root supplies the walking that came before.
senses.whyCN: 否定前缀去掉了「先前的例子」，词根则提供了「走在前面」的动作。

senses.title: An event with no earlier occurrence
senses.definition: an occurrence that has no previous instance in the record
senses.definitionCN: 在记录中找不到先前实例的事件
senses.example: The resignation was an unprecedented event in the company's history.
senses.exampleCN: 这次辞职在公司历史上是史无前例的事件。
senses.why: The word points to the record book: nothing on the earlier pages matches this page.
senses.whyCN: 这个词指向记录簿：前面几页没有任何内容与此页相符。

senses.title: A speed never seen before
senses.definition: a rate of change faster than any earlier measured rate
senses.definitionCN: 变化速度超过此前任何可测的速率
senses.example: The city grew at an unprecedented speed during those five years.
senses.exampleCN: 那五年里，这座城市以未曾有过的速度扩张。
senses.why: Speed is the dimension most often called unprecedented, because records measure it precisely.
senses.whyCN: 速度是这个词最常修饰的维度，因为记录能精确测量它。

senses.title: Demand or growth beyond all past peaks
senses.definition: a level of demand, growth or pressure higher than every earlier peak
senses.definitionCN: 需求、增长或压力高于此前每一个峰值
senses.example: The port handled unprecedented demand after the storm.
senses.exampleCN: 风暴过后，港口承接了空前的需求。
senses.why: Economists use the word when a curve passes every earlier peak on the chart.
senses.whyCN: 当曲线越过图表上此前每一个峰值，经济学家就用这个词。

senses.title: A ruling with no legal precedent
senses.definition: a decision for which earlier courts or rules provide no model
senses.definitionCN: 此前的判例或规则无法提供范本的裁决
senses.example: The tribunal issued an unprecedented ruling on digital ownership.
senses.exampleCN: 该法庭就数字财产所有权作出了无先例可循的裁决。
senses.why: Law is built on precedent, so a case without one is formally exceptional.
senses.whyCN: 法律建立在先例之上，因此没有先例的案件在形式上就是例外。

senses.title: A rare and extreme natural event
senses.definition: a weather or natural event outside every earlier record for the place
senses.definitionCN: 超出一个地方此前全部记录的天气或自然事件
senses.example: Forecasters called the drought unprecedented for the region.
senses.exampleCN: 预报员称这场干旱是该地区前所未有的。
senses.why: Weather records are long and numeric, which makes the claim testable.
senses.whyCN: 气象记录漫长且数字化，因此这一说法可以被检验。

senses.title: A record-breaking performance
senses.definition: a result that surpasses every previous mark in a sport or field
senses.definitionCN: 超过某项运动或领域此前所有标记的成绩
senses.example: Her unprecedented run broke three national records.
senses.exampleCN: 她前所未有的这一跑打破了三项全国纪录。
senses.why: Sport gives the word a stopwatch and a scoreboard, where being first is measurable.
senses.whyCN: 体育给了这个词一块秒表和一块记分牌，在那里「第一次」是可以测量的。

senses.title: A break with established practice
senses.definition: an action that departs from the usual custom or procedure
senses.definitionCN: 偏离通常惯例或程序的行为
senses.example: The mayor took the unprecedented step of publishing the budget draft.
senses.exampleCN: 市长采取了公布预算草案这一打破常规的做法。
senses.why: Custom, not nature, is the baseline here; the new move has simply never been tried.
senses.whyCN: 这里的基线是惯例而非自然；这一新做法只是从未被尝试过。

senses.title: Something a person has never experienced
senses.definition: an experience outside the whole range of one person's earlier life
senses.definitionCN: 超出一个人此前全部生活范围的经历
senses.example: For the young teacher, the attention was unprecedented.
senses.exampleCN: 对这位年轻教师来说，这样的关注是前所未有的。
senses.why: The record can be personal as well as public: a single life also has earlier pages.
senses.whyCN: 记录既可以是公共的，也可以是个人的：一个人的生活同样有前面的页。

intro.en: Unprecedented is a negative prefix laid over a Latin verb for going before: no earlier case has gone ahead to show the way.
intro.cn: 这个词是一个否定前缀加在一个表示「走在前面」的拉丁动词上：没有先前的例子先走过、指出道路。

items.en: cedere meant to go, to yield, to move along; it is the walking root inside the word.
items.cn: cedere 意为「走、让、前行」，是这个词内部的「行走」词根。

items.en: prae- meant before, so praecedere was to go before someone or something.
items.cn: prae- 表示「在前」，因此 praecedere 意为「走在某人或某物前面」。

items.en: The participle praecedens described what comes first, and English took it as precedent.
items.cn: 分词 praecedens 描述先出现的事物，英语把它借作 precedent。

items.en: A precedent is an earlier case used as a model; the word settled into law and general usage.
items.cn: 先例是被当作范本的先前案例；这个词在法律与一般用法中固定下来。

items.en: The negative prefix denies the existence of such a model, and the adjective ending attaches it to the case at hand.
items.cn: 否定前缀否认存在这样的范本，形容词词尾把它挂到眼前的案件上。

items.en: Statistics, journalism and sport made the adjective a standard way to say that the record book has no matching page.
items.cn: 统计、新闻与体育让这个形容词成为「记录簿里没有相符的一页」的标准说法。

note.en: The first group shares the going-before root or form; the second group names nearby ideas of being beyond all earlier examples.
note.cn: 第一组共享「走在前面」的词根或形音；第二组是与「超出此前所有例子」意思相邻的说法。

entries.definition: An earlier case or decision used as a guide; the noun that the negative adjective denies.
entries.definitionCN: 指被当作指南的先前案例或裁决；正是这个否定形容词所否认的名词。

entries.definition: To come or go before something else in time or order.
entries.definitionCN: 指在时间或顺序上先于某物。

entries.definition: The right to go first, or priority in rank or order.
entries.definitionCN: 指优先前行的权利，或地位、次序上的优先。

entries.definition: In a manner that has never occurred before.
entries.definitionCN: 以从未发生过的方式。

entries.definition: Free from bias; it looks close but its root is judging in advance, not going before.
entries.definitionCN: 指没有偏见的；形近，但其词根是「预先判断」，而非「走在前面」。

entries.definition: Having no equal in quality or degree; it stresses unmatched rank rather than a missing earlier case.
entries.definitionCN: 指质量或程度上无可匹敌；强调无与伦比，而非缺少先例。

entries.definition: Surpassing a measured mark; it is narrower and always tied to a recorded figure.
entries.definitionCN: 指超过某个已测标记；范围更窄，且总与记录数字相连。

entries.definition: New and original; it stresses freshness rather than the absence of any earlier instance.
entries.definitionCN: 指新颖独创；强调新鲜，而非完全没有先前实例。

entries.definition: Being the only one of its kind; it stresses singularity, not historical record.
entries.definitionCN: 指同类中唯一；强调独一无二，而非历史记录。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations use the real Latin go-before image, the real legal idea of precedent, and the real record phrases.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想使用真实的拉丁「走在前面」意象、真实的法律先例概念，以及真实的记录搭配。

normal.en: pre- means before and cedere means go: a precedent is a case that walked ahead of you.
normal.cn: pre- 是「在前」，cedere 是「走」：先例就是走在你前面的案例。

normal.en: Add un- and no case has walked ahead; the road has never been walked.
normal.cn: 加上 un-，就没有案例走在前头；这条路从未有人走过。

normal.en: Unprecedented scale, unprecedented demand and unprecedented event are three real phrases.
normal.cn: 空前的规模、空前的需求与史无前例的事件是三个真实搭配。

normal.en: Law lives on precedent, so a case without one is professionally shocking.
normal.cn: 法律靠先例生活，因此没有先例的案件在专业上令人震动。

normal.en: The word says nothing about quality, only about the empty earlier pages.
normal.cn: 这个词不评价好坏，只说前面的页是空的。

abstract.en: A record book is a promise that the future will resemble the past; this word announces that it did not.
abstract.cn: 记录簿是一份「未来会像过去」的承诺；这个词宣布它没有兑现。

abstract.en: Unprecedented does not mean better, only unmatched; the first of anything can be the worst.
abstract.cn: 前所未有并不意味着更好，只意味着无从比对；任何「第一次」都可能是最糟的一次。

abstract.en: Every unprecedented event becomes a precedent the moment it is written down.
abstract.cn: 每一个史无前例的事件，在被写下的那一刻就成了先例。

examples.en: The city is preparing for an unprecedented number of visitors this summer.
examples.cn: 这座城市正在为今夏前所未有的游客数量做准备。

examples.en: Scientists described the collapse of the ice shelf as unprecedented in the satellite record.
examples.cn: 科学家称冰架的崩塌在卫星记录中前所未有。

examples.en: The committee took the unprecedented step of reopening the hearing.
examples.cn: 委员会采取了重新开启听证会这一史无前例的举动。

dict_mnemonic.text: 读作「安普瑞西登提德」——前面没有任何「先例」走过

root: 由否定前缀 un- + precedent + 形容词词尾 -ed 构成；precedent 来自拉丁语 praecedere「走在前面」← prae-「在前」+ cedere「走、让」，分词 praecedens。词源链清楚。

sensesIntro.en: Nine senses run from a scale and an event with no earlier case through speed, demand, law, weather, sport and custom to one person's private experience.
sensesIntro.cn: 九个义项从没有先前例子的规模与事件，经过速度、需求、法律、天气、体育与惯例，最后落到一个人的私人经历。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: rows of old marks on a wall all sit low, and the new water stain rises above every one.
core.cn: 核心意象：墙上旧刻线都低低一排，新水痕却高过其中每一条。

branches.en: THE FIRST PAGE: a scale and an event for which the record book is blank.
branches.cn: 第一页：规模与事件在记录簿上都是空白。

branches.en: THE FAST CURVE: speed and demand that pass every earlier peak.
branches.cn: 陡峭曲线：速度与需求越过此前每个峰值。

branches.en: THE EMPTY CASE LAW: a ruling with no earlier court to follow.
branches.cn: 空白判例：裁决没有先前的法庭可循。

branches.en: THE EXTREME MARK: weather beyond the archive and a score beyond the board.
branches.cn: 极端标记：天气超出档案，成绩超出记分牌。

branches.en: THE UNTRIED MOVE: a custom broken and a life that has never met this before.
branches.cn: 未试之举：被打破的惯例，以及一个人从未遇到过的经历。

intro.en: Unprecedented is a negative prefix, a prefix meaning before, a walking root and an adjective ending stacked in one word.
intro.cn: 这个词把否定前缀、表「在前」的前缀、「行走」词根与形容词词尾叠在一个词里。

latinIntro.en: Latin supplies cedere and praecedere; English adds precedent, then un- and -ed to deny any earlier model.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语提供了 cedere 与 praecedere；英语先构成 precedent，再加 un- 与 -ed 否认任何先前范本。

items.example: It denies the existence of the earlier case.
items.exampleCN: 它否认先前案例的存在。

items.example: It sets the direction of the walking.
items.exampleCN: 它规定「走」的方向。

items.example: The root supplies movement.
items.exampleCN: 词根提供移动。

items.example: Prefix and root form the key verb.
items.exampleCN: 前缀与词根合成关键动词。

items.example: It becomes the English noun precedent.
items.exampleCN: 它变成英语名词 precedent。

items.example: The noun is what un- denies.
items.exampleCN: 这个名词正是 un- 所否认的。

items.example: It turns the noun into the adjective.
items.exampleCN: 它把名词变成形容词。

items.example: The verb keeps the walking image.
items.exampleCN: 动词保留行走意象。

items.example: The noun of rank uses the same root.
items.exampleCN: 表次序的名词使用同一词根。

derivatives.zh: 由前缀与词根构成，义为「先例」
同词根动词，义为「先于」
由现在分词构成，义为「在前的」
由表次序词尾构成，义为「优先」
由本词加副词词尾构成，义为「前所未有地」

definition_zh: 无处不在的；普遍存在的；广泛分布的；无孔不入的
definition_en: present, seen or found almost everywhere at the same time, so that no single place can be named as an exception
core_image: 一张城市地图上，同一个蓝色小点被盖在每一条街道、每一座车站和每一家店里
scene: 街角、地铁站、便利店门口，几乎每面墙上都贴着同一个蓝色标识，转角又是一张。Smartphones have become ubiquitous in daily life.
sceneCN: 这里指某样东西到处都能见到（第 1 个义项：无处不在）；句意为智能手机在日常生活中已无处不在。图中可辨识物件：城市地图、遍布各处的蓝色标识、地铁站与便利店。

pos.zh: 无处不在的；普遍存在的；广泛分布的

derivatives.zh: 由同一词根加表示状态的名词词尾构成，义为「无处不在；普遍存在」
由形容词加副词词尾构成，义为「无处不在地」
由形容词加表示性质的名词词尾构成，义为「无处不在的性质」
由同一词根加生物化学名词词尾构成，义为「泛素」，因广泛存在于真核细胞而得名

senses.title: Present almost everywhere
senses.definition: found in nearly every place at the same time
senses.definitionCN: 几乎在同一时间出现在每一个地方
senses.example: Smartphones have become ubiquitous in daily life.
senses.exampleCN: 智能手机在日常生活中已无处不在。
senses.why: The Latin source literally says everywhere, and the adjective keeps that flat, total coverage.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁来源字面意思就是「到处」，形容词保留了这种平铺的、全覆盖的含义。

senses.title: A widespread phenomenon
senses.definition: a condition or practice common across many places and groups
senses.definitionCN: 在许多地方与群体中普遍存在的状况或做法
senses.example: Social media use is now ubiquitous among teenagers.
senses.exampleCN: 社交媒体的使用如今在青少年中普遍存在。
senses.why: When a behaviour appears in every sample, the word describes a pattern rather than an object.
senses.whyCN: 当一种行为出现在每个样本里，这个词描述的就是模式，而非物件。

senses.title: A name or product everyone knows
senses.titleCN: 家喻户晓的品牌与产品
senses.definition: so widely distributed in culture that almost everyone recognizes it
senses.definitionCN: 在文化中分布极广，几乎人人都认得
senses.example: The brand became ubiquitous after one viral advertisement.
senses.exampleCN: 一支爆红的广告之后，这个品牌变得家喻户晓。
senses.why: Commerce uses the word for visibility: the logo is not just common but unavoidable.
senses.whyCN: 商业用这个词描述可见度：标识不只是常见，而是避不开。

senses.title: Technology embedded in every device
senses.definition: built into so many devices and settings that its presence is taken for granted
senses.definitionCN: 被装进太多设备与场景，以致其存在被视为理所当然
senses.example: Sensors are ubiquitous in modern buildings.
senses.exampleCN: 传感器在现代建筑中无处不在。
senses.why: Computing gave the word a technical home: the machine is no longer a place you go to.
senses.whyCN: 计算领域给了这个词一个技术归宿：机器不再是一个你要去的地方。

senses.title: A problem found in every corner
senses.definition: a fault or difficulty that appears across many unrelated settings
senses.definitionCN: 出现在许多互不相关的场景中的缺陷或困难
senses.example: Bias in hiring is ubiquitous, though it takes different forms.
senses.exampleCN: 招聘中的偏见无处不在，只是形式不同。
senses.why: The word can carry a warning: what is everywhere is also hard to notice.
senses.whyCN: 这个词可以带警告：到处都有的东西，也最难被察觉。

senses.title: Signs and messages everywhere
senses.titleCN: 到处出现的标识与信息
senses.definition: advertising or notices distributed so densely that they fill the visual field
senses.definitionCN: 广告或告示密集分布，占满视野
senses.example: Advertising screens are ubiquitous in the shopping district.
senses.exampleCN: 购物区里广告屏幕无处不在。
senses.why: The physical city can be covered, and the adjective describes that coverage.
senses.whyCN: 物理城市可以被覆盖，这个形容词描述的就是这种覆盖。

senses.title: A species found across habitats
senses.definition: occurring across many habitats or regions rather than in one niche
senses.definitionCN: 出现在许多栖息地或地区，而非局限于一个生态位
senses.example: The weed is ubiquitous along the riverbank.
senses.exampleCN: 这种杂草沿河岸广泛分布。
senses.why: Ecology uses the word for range, not for number: a rare animal can still be widespread.
senses.whyCN: 生态学用这个词描述分布范围，而非数量：稀少的动物也可以是广布的。

senses.title: Influence that cannot be escaped
senses.definition: an influence or system so extensive that no area of life remains outside it
senses.definitionCN: 影响或系统扩展到没有任何生活领域在其之外
senses.example: The platform's influence is ubiquitous in local news.
senses.exampleCN: 该平台对本地新闻的影响无孔不入。
senses.why: Here the word turns from description to critique: total presence begins to feel like pressure.
senses.whyCN: 这时词从描述转向批评：全面的存在开始让人感到压迫。

senses.title: Service available at any time and place
senses.definition: access to a service that no longer depends on a fixed location
senses.definitionCN: 获取某项服务不再依赖固定地点
senses.example: Wireless access is now ubiquitous on campus.
senses.exampleCN: 无线网络如今在校园里随处可得。
senses.why: Networks made availability a background condition, which is what the word describes best.
senses.whyCN: 网络让可用性成为一种背景条件，这正是这个词最擅长描述的。

intro.en: Ubiquitous is Latin for everywhere pressed into one adjective: a root meaning where, a particle meaning ever, and an adjective ending.
intro.cn: 这个词是拉丁语「到处」压成一个形容词：一个表示「哪里」的词根、一个表示「无论」的小品词，加一个形容词词尾。

items.en: ubi meant where, the plain interrogative and relative place word.
items.cn: ubi 意为「哪里」，是最普通的地点疑问词与关系词。

items.en: -que was an enclitic meaning and, and in this combination it gave the sense of ever or any.
items.cn: -que 是表示「和」的附缀，在这一组合中给出「无论、任何」的意思。

items.en: ubique meant everywhere, in every place, and it was used adverbially in classical Latin.
items.cn: ubique 意为「到处、在每个地方」，在古典拉丁语中作副词使用。

items.en: The abstract noun ubiquitas named the state of being everywhere.
items.cn: 抽象名词 ubiquitas 命名「无处不在」的状态。

items.en: English formed the adjective in the nineteenth century; the first records are early nineteenth century and the exact year is not certain, but the Latin line is clear.
items.cn: 英语在十九世纪构成这个形容词；首见记录在十九世纪初，具体年份不确定，但拉丁来源线索清楚。

items.en: Networks and mobile devices made the old word newly literal, and computing adopted it as a technical term.
items.cn: 网络与移动设备让这个旧词重新变得字面化，计算领域把它采纳为技术术语。

note.en: The first group shares root or shape with ubiquitous; the second group names nearby ideas of wide presence and keeps their emphasis apart.
note.cn: 第一组在词根或形音上与 ubiquitous 相近；第二组是与「广泛存在」意思相邻的说法，说明中区分各自侧重。

entries.definition: The noun for the state of being everywhere at once.
entries.definitionCN: 指同时无处不在的状态。

entries.definition: The adverb describing action or presence that reaches every place.
entries.definitionCN: 副词，描述抵达每个地方的行动或存在。

entries.definition: A clumsy but real noun for the quality itself.
entries.definitionCN: 指这种性质本身的一个笨重但真实的名词。

entries.definition: A small protein found throughout eukaryotic cells, named for being everywhere.
entries.definitionCN: 指广泛存在于真核细胞中的一种小蛋白，因「到处都有」而得名。

entries.definition: Of one mind; it looks close but its root is one spirit, not every place.
entries.definitionCN: 指意见一致；形近，但其词根是「同一心意」，而非「每个地方」。

entries.definition: Common in a particular group, place or time; it stresses frequency within a setting, not presence in every setting.
entries.definitionCN: 指在特定群体、地方或时期常见；强调某一场景内的频率，而非每个场景都有。

entries.definition: Distributed over a large area or many people; it stresses breadth of distribution, not the absence of exceptions.
entries.definitionCN: 指分布在大片地区或许多人中；强调分布之广，而非没有例外。

entries.definition: Present everywhere at once, often with a sense of a watching or divine presence.
entries.definitionCN: 指同时存在于一切地方，常带被注视或神圣临在的意味。

entries.definition: Spreading through and filling every part of something; it stresses penetration rather than coverage.
entries.definitionCN: 指渗透并充满某物的每个部分；强调渗透，而非覆盖。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations use the real Latin where-and-ever parts, the real technology phrases and the real contrast with prevalence.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想使用真实的拉丁「哪里＋无论」构件、真实的技术搭配，以及与 prevalent 的真实区别。

normal.en: ubi means where and -que adds ever: ubique is wherever, so ubiquitous is everywhere.
normal.cn: ubi 是「哪里」，-que 加「无论」：ubique 是「无论哪里」，所以 ubiquitous 就是「到处」。

normal.en: A map with the same dot stamped on every street shows the word better than a sentence.
normal.cn: 一张在每条街都盖上同一个小点的地图，比一句话更能说明这个词。

normal.en: Ubiquitous technology, ubiquitous computing and ubiquitous access are three real phrases.
normal.cn: 无处不在的技术、普适计算与随时随地的访问是三个真实搭配。

normal.en: Prevalent means common in one setting; ubiquitous means no setting is without it.
normal.cn: prevalent 指在某一场景常见；ubiquitous 指没有一个场景缺少它。

normal.en: The noun ubiquity is the state, the adverb ubiquitously is the manner.
normal.cn: 名词 ubiquity 是状态，副词 ubiquitously 是方式。

abstract.en: What is everywhere stops being noticed; ubiquity is a kind of invisibility.
abstract.cn: 到处都有的东西不再被注意；无处不在是一种隐形。

abstract.en: A word for total coverage is also a word for no exit, which is why it can sound like a warning.
abstract.cn: 一个描述全面覆盖的词，也是描述无处可退的词，所以它听起来可能像警告。

abstract.en: The same adjective describes a helpful network and an unwanted gaze; presence itself is neutral.
abstract.cn: 同一个形容词既描述有用的网络，也描述不受欢迎的注视；存在本身是中性的。

examples.en: Plastic packaging is now ubiquitous in every supermarket aisle.
examples.cn: 塑料包装如今在每条超市货架间都随处可见。

examples.en: The composer's arrangements became ubiquitous in film scores of the period.
examples.cn: 这位作曲家的编曲在那个时期的电影配乐中无处不在。

examples.en: Cameras are so ubiquitous that visitors no longer notice them.
examples.cn: 摄像头多到无处不在，访客已不再注意到它们。

dict_mnemonic.text: 读作「尤比克维特斯」——拉丁语「无论哪里」压成一个词：到处都在

root: 来自拉丁语 ubique「到处」← ubi「哪里」+ -que「无论、和」，抽象名词 ubiquitas；英语在十九世纪加形容词词尾 -ous 构成 ubiquitous。来源链清楚，首见年份为约数。

sensesIntro.en: Nine senses run from simple everywhere-presence through phenomena, brands, devices, problems, signs, species and influence to round-the-clock availability.
sensesIntro.cn: 九个义项从简单的「到处都在」，经过现象、品牌、设备、问题、标识、物种与影响，最后落到全天候可得。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: one blue mark is stamped on every street of a city map until no blank space remains.
core.cn: 核心意象：一枚蓝印被盖在城市地图的每条街上，直到不留一点空白。

branches.en: THE PLAIN COVERAGE: an object or a practice found in every sample.
branches.cn: 朴素覆盖：物件或做法在每个样本中都出现。

branches.en: THE VISIBLE CITY: brands and signs that fill the visual field.
branches.cn: 可见的城市：品牌与标识占满视野。

branches.en: THE EMBEDDED NETWORK: sensors and access that no longer need a fixed place.
branches.cn: 嵌入的网络：传感器与访问不再依赖固定地点。

branches.en: THE PATTERN AND THE RANGE: a fault everywhere, a species across every habitat.
branches.cn: 模式与范围：到处都有的缺陷，跨越每种栖息地的物种。

branches.en: THE TOTAL GAZE: influence with no area left outside it.
branches.cn: 全面注视：没有任何领域留在其外的影响。

intro.en: Ubiquitous is three Latin pieces and one adjective ending: a place word, an ever particle, and a suffix of quality.
intro.cn: 这个词是三个拉丁部件加一个形容词词尾：一个地点词、一个「无论」小品词，以及一个表性质的词尾。

latinIntro.en: Latin supplies ubi, ubique and ubiquitas; English adds -ous to make the adjective.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语提供了 ubi、ubique 与 ubiquitas；英语加上 -ous 构成形容词。

items.example: The place question begins the word.
items.exampleCN: 地点疑问词开启了这个词。

items.example: It turns where into wherever.
items.exampleCN: 它把「哪里」变成「无论哪里」。

items.example: The adverb states total coverage.
items.exampleCN: 这个副词陈述全面覆盖。

items.example: The abstract noun names the quality.
items.exampleCN: 抽象名词命名这种性质。

items.example: It forms the English adjective.
items.exampleCN: 它构成英语形容词。

items.example: The noun drops the adjective ending for a state noun.
items.exampleCN: 名词去掉形容词词尾，换成状态名词。

items.example: It forms ubiquitously.
items.exampleCN: 它构成 ubiquitously。

items.example: It forms ubiquitousness.
items.exampleCN: 它构成 ubiquitousness。

items.example: It forms ubiquitin, named for wide presence.
items.exampleCN: 它构成 ubiquitin，因广泛存在而得名。

derivatives.zh: 由词根加状态名词词尾构成，义为「无处不在」
由形容词加副词词尾构成，义为「无处不在地」
由形容词加性质名词词尾构成，义为「无处不在的性质」
由词根加科学名词词尾构成，义为「泛素」

definition_zh: 多才多艺的；多用途的；适应性强的；多功能的；灵活的
definition_en: able to turn to many different skills, uses or roles instead of being fixed to one
core_image: 同一个人先后站在球场三个不同位置，脚边的战术板画着三条不同的跑位线
scene: 一名球员先踢前锋，又回撤中场，最后临时顶到后防线，教练在场边不断改画战术板。The coach valued her as a versatile player who could fill three positions.
sceneCN: 这里指一个人能胜任多个位置与角色（第 1 个义项：多才多艺、能担多职）；句意为教练看重她这名能踢三个位置的多面手。图中可辨识物件：足球场、三个不同站位、不断改画的战术板。

pos.zh: 多才多艺的；多用途的；适应性强的

derivatives.zh: 由形容词加表示性质的名词词尾构成，义为「多才多艺；多用途」
由形容词加副词词尾构成，义为「以多用途的方式」，较少使用

senses.title: Able to take many roles
senses.definition: of a person, able to perform well in several different positions or jobs
senses.definitionCN: 指一个人能在多个不同位置或工作中都表现良好
senses.example: The coach valued her as a versatile player who could fill three positions.
senses.exampleCN: 教练看重她这名能踢三个位置的多面手。
senses.why: The Latin adjective meant turning about; a person who can turn to a new role keeps that motion.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁形容词意为「能转动的」；一个人能转向新角色，就保留了这种转动。

senses.title: Serving many purposes
senses.definition: of a tool or material, useful for a wide range of tasks
senses.definitionCN: 指工具或材料可用于很广的一类任务
senses.example: A versatile knife is the only tool the campers carry.
senses.exampleCN: 一把多用途小刀是露营者唯一携带的工具。
senses.why: An object cannot choose a role, yet it can be turned to many uses, which is the same picture.
senses.whyCN: 物件不会自己选角色，却能转向很多用途，这正是同一幅图景。

senses.title: Adaptable to new conditions
senses.definition: able to adjust quickly to changed demands or settings
senses.definitionCN: 能迅速适应变化了的要求或环境
senses.example: The versatile crew could work both on deck and in the engine room.
senses.exampleCN: 这支适应性强的船员队伍既能在甲板工作，也能进机舱。
senses.why: Adaptation is turning in place: the same ability meets an unfamiliar demand.
senses.whyCN: 适应就是原地转向：同一种能力去应对陌生的要求。

senses.title: Multi-function in design
senses.definition: combining several functions in one device, space or system
senses.definitionCN: 把多种功能合在一个设备、空间或系统中
senses.example: The versatile studio works as a classroom by day and a rehearsal hall by night.
senses.exampleCN: 这间多功能工作室白天当教室，晚上当排练厅。
senses.why: Architecture uses the word for a room that can be turned to a second purpose without rebuilding.
senses.whyCN: 建筑学用这个词指一间不必重建就能转向第二种用途的房间。

senses.title: Wide-ranging in style or skill
senses.definition: showing a broad range of styles or techniques rather than one narrow speciality
senses.definitionCN: 展现广泛风格或技法，而非一门狭窄专长
senses.example: Her versatile voice moved easily between folk song and jazz.
senses.exampleCN: 她多面的嗓音在民谣与爵士之间自如转换。
senses.why: The word praises range itself, not just the ability to switch tasks.
senses.whyCN: 这个词赞赏的是广度本身，而不只是能换任务。

senses.title: Useful across many jobs
senses.definition: of an employee, able to cover several functions in one organisation
senses.definitionCN: 指雇员能在一个组织里承担多项职能
senses.example: Small firms prefer versatile staff who can cover two desks.
senses.exampleCN: 小公司偏爱能顶两个岗位的多面手员工。
senses.why: Employment turns versatility into an economic asset: fewer people, more roles.
senses.whyCN: 雇佣关系把「多面」变成经济资产：更少的人，更多的角色。

senses.title: Flexible in layout or use
senses.definition: of a space or plan, open to more than one arrangement
senses.definitionCN: 指空间或方案可以容纳不止一种安排
senses.example: The versatile floor plan allowed the tenants to combine two units.
senses.exampleCN: 灵活的平面布局让租户可以把两个单元合并。
senses.why: The turning is now spatial: walls and uses can be rearranged.
senses.whyCN: 这里的转动是空间性的：墙体与用途都可以重新排列。

senses.title: Able to think along many lines
senses.titleCN: 思路灵活、能多角度思考
senses.definition: of a mind, able to approach a problem from several directions
senses.definitionCN: 指头脑能从多个方向接近一个问题
senses.example: A versatile thinker is hard to surprise in a debate.
senses.exampleCN: 思路灵活的人在辩论中很难被出其不意。
senses.why: The metaphor moves inward: what turns is not the body but the line of thought.
senses.whyCN: 这个比喻转向内部：转动的不是身体，而是思路。

senses.title: An all-round athlete
senses.definition: of an athlete, competitive across several events or disciplines
senses.definitionCN: 指运动员能在多个项目或分项中竞争
senses.example: The versatile gymnast qualified for four different finals.
senses.exampleCN: 这位全能型体操选手晋级了四个不同的决赛。
senses.why: Sport gives versatility a scoreboard: the all-rounder is measured across events.
senses.whyCN: 体育给「多面」配了记分牌：全能选手跨项目被测量。

intro.en: Versatile is a Latin adjective for something that turns, from a verb meaning to keep turning; English extended the image from objects to people and skills.
intro.cn: 这个词是拉丁语中表示「会转动的」形容词，来自意为「不断转动」的动词；英语把这一意象从物件扩展到人与技能。

items.en: vertere meant to turn, to turn around, and it is the root of version, convert and many more.
items.cn: vertere 意为「转、使转向」，是 version、convert 等许多词的词根。

items.en: versare was a frequentative form, suggesting repeated or restless turning.
items.cn: versare 是反复态形式，暗示反复或不停地转动。

items.en: versatilis described a thing that can be turned about, hence adaptable.
items.cn: versatilis 描述可以被转来转去的东西，因此引申为「可适应的」。

items.en: French passed the adjective to English in the sixteenth century; the earliest records are approximate in date but the source line is clear.
items.cn: 法语在十六世纪把这个形容词传给英语；最早记录的具体年份为约数，但来源线索清楚。

items.en: English extended a word about turning objects to people who can turn to many skills.
items.cn: 英语把原本描述物体转动的词，扩展用于能转向多种技能的人。

items.en: Design and sport now use the adjective for multi-function rooms and all-round athletes.
items.cn: 设计与体育如今用这个形容词指多功能空间与全能运动员。

note.en: The first group shares the turning root or looks close; the second group names nearby kinds of flexibility. Note the double layer: versatile describes both a person with many skills and an object with many uses, and the near words usually cover only one of those layers.
note.cn: 第一组共享「转动」词根或形音相近；第二组是邻近的灵活类说法。注意双层：versatile 既指人有多种本领，也指物有多种用途，而邻近词通常只覆盖其中一层。

entries.definition: The noun for the quality of serving many purposes or roles.
entries.definitionCN: 指多用途或多角色的性质。

entries.definition: Skilled or experienced in a subject; it comes from the same turning verb but stresses training.
entries.definitionCN: 指精通或熟悉某领域；同一「转动」动词而来，但强调训练有素。

entries.definition: One form of something that has been turned or translated.
entries.definitionCN: 指某物经过转写或翻译后的一种形式。

entries.definition: To turn something into another form or use.
entries.definitionCN: 指把某物转成另一种形式或用途。

entries.definition: Easily changing or evaporating; it looks close but comes from a flying root, not a turning one.
entries.definitionCN: 指易变或易挥发；形近，但来自「飞」的词根，而非「转」。

entries.definition: Standing upright; it shares the turning root through the idea of a turning point or summit.
entries.definitionCN: 指垂直的；经由「转向点、顶点」的概念共享同一词根。

entries.definition: Able to change to fit new conditions; it stresses adjustment rather than range of uses.
entries.definitionCN: 指能改变以适应新条件；强调调整，而非用途之广。

entries.definition: Able to bend or be changed without breaking; it stresses elasticity and willingness to adjust.
entries.definitionCN: 指能弯曲或改变而不折断；强调弹性与愿意变通。

entries.definition: Good at many things rather than specialising; it is warmer and more colloquial for people.
entries.definitionCN: 指多方面都好而不专精；用于人时更亲切、更口语。

entries.definition: Having many sides or aspects; it describes complexity rather than practical use.
entries.definitionCN: 指具有许多侧面或面向；描述复杂性，而非实用多能。

entries.definition: Designed for several uses; it covers the object layer of versatile but says nothing about a person's skills.
entries.definitionCN: 指为多种用途设计；只覆盖本词的「物」这一层，不涉及人的本领。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations use the real Latin turning image, the real object and person pairs, and the real contrast with volatile.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想使用真实的拉丁「转动」意象、真实的物件与人的双重用法，以及与 volatile 的真实区别。

normal.en: The root means turn: a versatile person can turn from one role to another without losing balance.
normal.cn: 词根意为「转」：多才多艺的人能从一种角色转到另一种，而不失衡。

normal.en: The same adjective fits a knife with many blades and a player with many positions.
normal.cn: 同一个形容词既适合多刀口的小刀，也适合能踢多个位置的球员。

normal.en: Versatile player, versatile tool and versatile material are three real phrases.
normal.cn: 多面手球员、多用途工具与多用途材料是三个真实搭配。

normal.en: Versatility is the noun; turn the adjective into a quality and you have it.
normal.cn: versatility 是名词；把形容词变成一种性质就得到它。

normal.en: Do not confuse turning with flying: volatile is the word built on flight.
normal.cn: 别把「转」和「飞」混了：volatile 是建立在「飞行」上的词。

abstract.en: Versatility is not knowing everything; it is refusing to be only one thing.
abstract.cn: 多才多艺不是无所不知，而是拒绝只做一样东西。

abstract.en: A tool with many uses is also a tool with no single identity, which is both its freedom and its cost.
abstract.cn: 多用途的工具也是没有单一身份的工具，这既是自由，也是代价。

abstract.en: The turning image suggests balance: turn too far and the versatile becomes merely scattered.
abstract.cn: 转动的意象暗示平衡：转得太远，多面就变成了散乱。

examples.en: The workshop needs a versatile technician who can handle both wiring and plumbing.
examples.cn: 车间需要一名既能处理电路又能处理水管的万能技师。

examples.en: Bamboo is a versatile material for furniture, scaffolding and paper.
examples.cn: 竹子是可用于家具、脚手架和纸张的多用途材料。

examples.en: Her versatile style made her the obvious choice for the opening act.
examples.cn: 她多面的风格使她成为开场表演的当然人选。

dict_mnemonic.text: 读作「佛赛头」——能转来转去，样样都能上手

root: 来自拉丁语 versatilis「可转动的、可变通的」← versare「反复转动」← vertere「转」，经法语于十六世纪进入英语。来源链清楚，首见年份为约数。

sensesIntro.en: Nine senses run from a person with many roles through tools, adaptation, design, style, employment, space and thought to an all-round athlete.
sensesIntro.cn: 九个义项从能担多职的人，经过工具、适应、设计、风格、雇佣、空间与思维，最后落到全能运动员。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: one body stands in three different positions on the same pitch, each with its own line of movement.
core.cn: 核心意象：同一具身体在同一片球场上站过三个位置，每个位置都有各自的跑动线。

branches.en: THE PERSON: roles, styles and events that one performer can cover.
branches.cn: 人：一个表演者能覆盖的角色、风格与项目。

branches.en: THE OBJECT: a tool or a room turned to more than one purpose.
branches.cn: 物：被转向不止一种用途的工具或房间。

branches.en: THE WORKING LIFE: a crew or employee who adapts to new demands.
branches.cn: 工作生涯：适应新要求的班组或员工。

branches.en: THE PLAN: a layout open to more than one arrangement.
branches.cn: 方案：可容纳不止一种安排的布局。

branches.en: THE MIND: a line of thought that can turn to another angle.
branches.cn: 心智：能转向另一角度的思路。

intro.en: Versatile is a Latin turning verb plus an adjective ending meaning able to be.
intro.cn: 这个词是一个拉丁「转动」动词加一个表示「能被……的」形容词词尾。

latinIntro.en: Latin supplies vertere, versare and versatilis; the English noun versatility adds a quality ending.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语提供了 vertere、versare 与 versatilis；英语名词 versatility 再加一个性质词尾。

items.example: The root supplies the turning.
items.exampleCN: 词根提供「转动」。

items.example: The frequentative form adds motion.
items.exampleCN: 反复态形式加上持续运动。

items.example: The adjective means adaptable.
items.exampleCN: 这个形容词意为「可适应的」。

items.example: It marks capacity.
items.exampleCN: 它标记能力。

items.example: The borrowed adjective keeps the motion.
items.exampleCN: 借入的形容词保留运动。

items.example: It forms versatility.
items.exampleCN: 它构成 versatility。

items.example: It forms versatilely, a rare adverb.
items.exampleCN: 它构成较少用的副词 versatilely。

items.example: The same root gives the facing word.
items.exampleCN: 同一词根给出表示「相对」的词。

items.example: A sister word keeps the turning.
items.exampleCN: 同族词保留「转动」。
