由形容词加副词词尾构成，义为「以多用途方式」

definition_zh: 能存活的；可行的；可实施的；能维持的；有生存力的
definition_en: able to stay alive, or able to work and continue successfully in practice
core_image: 一株幼苗顶开土面站稳，旁边一只空壳种子倒在土里，记录牌上画着发芽曲线
scene: 温室里，一株幼苗顶开土面，叶片慢慢展开，旁边另一粒种子却始终没有动静。Only two of the seeds were viable after the long drought.
sceneCN: 这里指种子具有存活发芽的能力（第 1 个义项：能存活、能生长）；句意为漫长干旱之后只有两粒种子还能存活。图中可辨识物件：幼苗、未发芽的种子、育苗盘、记录牌。

pos.zh: 能存活的；可行的；可维持的

derivatives.zh: 由形容词加表示能力的名词词尾构成，义为「存活能力；可行性」
由形容词加副词词尾构成，义为「以可行的方式」
由否定前缀加本词构成，义为「不能存活的；不可行的」

senses.title: Able to stay alive
senses.definition: of a living thing, seed or cell, able to live and grow under present conditions
senses.definitionCN: 指生物、种子或细胞在现有条件下能够存活并生长
senses.example: Only two of the seeds were viable after the long drought.
senses.exampleCN: 漫长干旱之后，只有两粒种子还能存活。
senses.why: The French source joins a word for life to a suffix of ability, so the first sense is simply able to live.
senses.whyCN: 法语来源把一个表示「生命」的词接上表能力的词尾，因此第一义就是「能活」。

senses.title: Able to be carried out
senses.definition: of a plan or method, practical enough to be put into effect
senses.definitionCN: 指计划或方法足够实际，可以付诸实施
senses.example: The engineers proposed a viable route around the flooded valley.
senses.exampleCN: 工程师提出了一条绕开被淹山谷的可行路线。
senses.why: The word moved from organisms to plans: what can survive contact with reality is viable.
senses.whyCN: 这个词从生物转到计划：经得起现实接触的，就是可行的。

senses.title: Able to survive financially
senses.definition: of a business or project, able to cover its costs and keep operating
senses.definitionCN: 指企业或项目能覆盖成本并持续运转
senses.example: The farm became viable only after it switched to direct sales.
senses.exampleCN: 这家农场直到改做直销才变得能维持下去。
senses.why: Money is the environment in which a business lives or dies, so the metaphor stays biological.
senses.whyCN: 金钱是企业生死存亡的环境，因此这个比喻仍是生物学的。

senses.title: Able to keep an organisation alive
senses.definition: of an institution or industry, strong enough to continue rather than collapse
senses.definitionCN: 指机构或行业足够强健，能继续存在而不崩溃
senses.example: Analysts asked whether the small airline was still viable.
senses.exampleCN: 分析人士追问这家小航空公司是否仍有生存力。
senses.why: Here viability is about the whole body, not a single plan or budget line.
senses.whyCN: 这里的生存力关乎整个机体，而非单一计划或一条预算。

senses.title: Able to continue as a tradition
senses.definition: of a custom, language or system, likely to survive into the future
senses.definitionCN: 指习俗、语言或制度有可能延续到未来
senses.example: Few believed the village school was still viable with so few children.
senses.exampleCN: 很少有人相信，孩子这么少，村校还能办得下去。
senses.why: The metaphor extends to anything that must renew itself to last.
senses.whyCN: 这个比喻扩展到任何必须自我更新才能延续的事物。

senses.title: A practical substitute
senses.titleCN: 可实际采用的替代方案
senses.definition: of an alternative, realistic enough to replace what is currently used
senses.definitionCN: 指替代方案足够现实，可以取代当前所用之物
senses.example: Solar power is now a viable alternative to diesel in remote areas.
senses.exampleCN: 在偏远地区，太阳能如今是柴油的可行替代方案。
senses.why: A substitute must survive comparison, which is why the word so often sits before alternative.
senses.whyCN: 替代品必须经得起比较，所以这个词常放在「替代方案」前面。

senses.title: Able to reproduce and persist
senses.definition: of a population, large enough and healthy enough to breed and persist
senses.definitionCN: 指种群规模与健康程度足以繁殖并持续存在
senses.example: Conservationists set a target for a viable population of the species.
senses.exampleCN: 保护工作者为该物种设定了可存续种群的目标。
senses.why: Ecology makes viability a property of a group, not of one organism.
senses.whyCN: 生态学把「可存活」变成群体的属性，而非单个生物的属性。

senses.title: Acceptable in political or legal terms
senses.definition: of a proposal, able to win acceptance without being rejected outright
senses.definitionCN: 指提案能被接受，而不会被直接否决
senses.example: The reform was technically sound but not politically viable.
senses.exampleCN: 这项改革在技术上站得住，但在政治上行不通。
senses.why: A proposal also lives in an environment: it must survive the room it is presented to.
senses.whyCN: 提案也生活在环境里：它必须熬过被提交的那个房间。

senses.title: A candidate with a real chance
senses.definition: of a person in a contest, having a realistic chance of success
senses.definitionCN: 指竞争中有现实成功机会的人
senses.example: Party leaders looked for a viable candidate in the northern district.
senses.exampleCN: 党内领导层在北部选区寻找有胜算的候选人。
senses.why: A candidacy is another life that must survive the contest to continue.
senses.whyCN: 候选资格是另一种必须熬过竞争才能延续的生命。

intro.en: Viable joins a Latin word for life to a suffix meaning able to: the original sense is simply able to live, and English extended it to plans that can survive.
intro.cn: 这个词把拉丁语表示「生命」的词接上表「能够」的词尾：本义就是「能活」，英语再扩展到「能经得起现实」的计划。

items.en: vita meant life, and it is the stem behind vital and vitality as well.
items.cn: vita 意为「生命」，也是 vital 与 vitality 的词干。

items.en: French shortened the Latin stem into vie, the everyday word for life.
items.cn: 法语把拉丁词干缩成 vie，即日常用语中的「生命」。

items.en: French built viable from vie plus a suffix of ability, first for a fetus able to live outside the womb.
items.cn: 法语用 vie 加表能力的词尾构成 viable，最初指胎儿能离开子宫存活。

items.en: English borrowed the adjective in the nineteenth century, first in the medical sense; the exact first date is approximate but the line is clear.
items.cn: 英语在十九世纪借入这个形容词，最初用于医学含义；具体首见年份为约数，但来源线索清楚。

items.en: The twentieth century extended it from organisms to projects, firms and proposals that can survive reality.
items.cn: 二十世纪把它从生物扩展到能在现实中存续的项目、企业与提案。

items.en: Policy and ecology now speak of viable alternatives and viable populations.
items.cn: 政策与生态学现在会说「可行的替代方案」与「可存续的种群」。

note.en: The first group shares the life root or looks close; the second group names nearby ideas of practicality, and the note separates viable from feasible.
note.cn: 第一组共享「生命」词根或形音相近；第二组是邻近的实用性说法，说明中把 viable 与 feasible 分开。

entries.definition: The noun for the ability to live or to succeed in practice.
entries.definitionCN: 指存活或实践中成功的能力。

entries.definition: The adverb for doing something in a way that can be sustained.
entries.definitionCN: 副词，指以可持续的方式做某事。

entries.definition: Not able to live or to work in practice.
entries.definitionCN: 指不能存活或在实践中行不通。

entries.definition: Necessary to life or to success; it shares the life stem but stresses necessity.
entries.definitionCN: 指对生命或成功必不可少；共享「生命」词干，但强调必要。

entries.definition: Likely to change; it looks close but comes from a root meaning to vary, not to live.
entries.definitionCN: 指易变的；形近，但词根意为「变化」，而非「生命」。

entries.definition: Possible to do with the means available; it asks whether a thing can be done, not whether it can live on.
entries.definitionCN: 指用现有手段可以做到；它问的是「能不能做」，而非「能不能活下去」。

entries.definition: Practical enough to operate; plainer and often about a method or arrangement.
entries.definitionCN: 指足够实用、能运转；更朴素，常指方法或安排。

entries.definition: Able to continue over time without exhausting its base; it stresses endurance, not first survival.
entries.definitionCN: 指能长期持续而不耗尽基础；强调持久，而非初次存活。

entries.definition: Alive now; for a fetus or organism it is the plain everyday word.
entries.definitionCN: 指当下活着的；用于胎儿或生物时是最朴素的说法。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations use the real life stem, the real medical origin and the real contrast with feasible.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想使用真实的「生命」词干、真实的医学起源，以及与 feasible 的真实区别。

normal.en: Vita is life and -able is able: viable is literally able to live, and a plan must also live.
normal.cn: vita 是生命，-able 是能够：viable 字面上就是「能活」，而计划也得活下去。

normal.en: A seed that sprouts and a business that pays its bills share one adjective.
normal.cn: 发芽的种子与付得起账的企业共享同一个形容词。

normal.en: Viable alternative, commercially viable and viable population are three real phrases.
normal.cn: 可行的替代方案、商业上可行与可存续种群是三个真实搭配。

normal.en: Feasible asks can it be done; viable asks can it stay alive after it is done.
normal.cn: feasible 问「做得成吗」；viable 问「做成之后活得下去吗」。

normal.en: The noun is viability, the negative is nonviable, and both keep the life image.
normal.cn: 名词是 viability，否定形式是 nonviable，两者都保留「生命」意象。

abstract.en: Viability is survival under present conditions, which means the conditions can always take it away.
abstract.cn: 可行性是在现有条件下存活，这意味着条件随时可以把它收回。

abstract.en: A plan is an organism in the environment of budgets, habits and politics.
abstract.cn: 计划是一个生活在预算、习惯与政治环境中的生物。

abstract.en: What is viable is not necessarily good; some harmful things survive very well.
abstract.cn: 能存活的不一定是好的；有些有害之物活得非常好。

examples.en: The clinic kept the premature infant in an incubator until it was viable.
examples.cn: 诊所把早产儿放在保温箱里，直到他能存活。

examples.en: Recycling becomes economically viable once collection is combined with other services.
examples.cn: 一旦把收集与其他服务合并，回收在经济上就变得可行。

examples.en: The party needed a viable candidate before it could contest the seat.
examples.cn: 该党需要一名有胜算的候选人，才能争夺这个席位。

dict_mnemonic.text: 读作「外尔伯」——「能活」；能活下来，才算可行

root: 来自法语 viable「能活的」← vie「生命」+ -able「能够」，vie 出自拉丁语 vita「生命」。英语十九世纪借入，先用于胎儿存活的医学含义。来源链清楚，首见年份为约数。

sensesIntro.en: Nine senses run from a living seed through plans, finances, institutions, traditions, substitutes, populations, politics and candidates.
sensesIntro.cn: 九个义项从能活的种子，经过计划、财务、机构、传统、替代方案、种群、政治与候选人。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: one seedling stands up out of the soil while the seed beside it stays shut.
core.cn: 核心意象：一株幼苗从土里立起来，旁边那粒种子却始终没有打开。

branches.en: THE ORGANISM: a seed, a fetus or a whole population that can keep living.
branches.cn: 生物：能继续存活的种子、胎儿或整个种群。

branches.en: THE PLAN AND THE SUBSTITUTE: a route or alternative that survives reality.
branches.cn: 计划与替代：经得起现实的路线或替代方案。

branches.en: THE MONEY AND THE INSTITUTION: a firm or industry that can cover its costs.
branches.cn: 钱与机构：能覆盖成本的企业或行业。

branches.en: THE TRADITION: a school, language or custom able to renew itself.
branches.cn: 传统：能自我更新的学校、语言或习俗。

branches.en: THE ROOM AND THE RACE: a proposal or candidate that can survive a vote.
branches.cn: 房间与竞赛：能熬过投票的提案或候选人。

intro.en: Viable is a life stem plus an ability suffix, borrowed whole from French.
intro.cn: 这个词是「生命」词干加表能力的词尾，整体借自法语。

latinIntro.en: Latin supplies vita and vitalis; French supplies vie and viable, and English took the French adjective.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语提供了 vita 与 vitalis；法语提供了 vie 与 viable，英语借入的是法语形容词。

items.example: The stem names life itself.
items.exampleCN: 这个词干命名生命本身。

items.example: The French form carries the stem forward.
items.exampleCN: 法语形式把词干传下去。

items.example: It supplies the capacity.
items.exampleCN: 它提供「能力」。

items.example: The borrowed word begins as a medical term.
items.exampleCN: 借入的词最初是医学术语。

items.meaning: the ability to live or work
items.example: The noun adds a quality ending.
items.exampleCN: 名词加上性质词尾。

items.example: A sister adjective keeps the life stem.
items.exampleCN: 同族形容词保留「生命」词干。

items.example: English keeps the sister sense.
items.exampleCN: 英语保留了同族含义。

items.example: It forms nonviable, the failed case.
items.exampleCN: 它构成 nonviable，即失败的情形。

items.example: It forms viably.
items.exampleCN: 它构成 viably。

derivatives.zh: 由形容词加能力名词词尾构成，义为「可行性」
由形容词加副词词尾构成，义为「以可行方式」
由否定前缀加本词构成，义为「不能存活的」

definition_zh: 易挥发的；易变的；不稳定的；易怒的；短暂易逝的；易失的
definition_en: evaporating quickly, or changing suddenly and unpredictably, or lasting only a short time
core_image: 敞口烧杯里的液体不断变少，一缕看不见的蒸气向上升，旁边行情屏幕上的曲线剧烈跳动
scene: 通风柜里，敞口烧杯中的透明液体几分钟就少了一半，柜门上的警示标签被风吹得微微翻起。The solvent is volatile and must be handled inside the fume hood.
sceneCN: 这里指液体容易挥发（第 1 个义项：易挥发）；句意为这种溶剂易挥发，必须在通风柜内操作。图中可辨识物件：通风柜、敞口烧杯、下降的液面、警示标签。

pos.zh: 易挥发的；易变的；不稳定的；易怒的

derivatives.zh: 由形容词加表示性质的名词词尾构成，义为「挥发性；波动性」
由形容词加表示「使……化」的动词词尾构成，义为「使挥发」
由挥发动词加动作名词词尾构成，义为「挥发过程」
由否定前缀加本词构成，义为「不挥发的；非易失的」

senses.title: Evaporating quickly
senses.definition: of a liquid or substance, turning into vapour rapidly at ordinary temperatures
senses.definitionCN: 指液体或物质在常温下迅速变成蒸气
senses.example: The solvent is volatile and must be handled inside the fume hood.
senses.exampleCN: 这种溶剂易挥发，必须在通风柜内操作。
senses.why: The Latin adjective meant flying; a liquid that flies off into the air keeps the literal image.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁形容词意为「会飞的」；飞进空气里的液体保留了字面意象。

senses.title: Moving unpredictably in price
senses.definition: of a market or price, rising and falling sharply without a stable trend
senses.definitionCN: 指市场或价格大起大落，没有稳定趋势
senses.example: Oil prices stayed volatile through the whole quarter.
senses.exampleCN: 整个季度油价都在剧烈波动。
senses.why: Finance borrowed the flying image: numbers that will not settle are numbers that keep taking off.
senses.whyCN: 金融借用了「飞」的意象：不肯落地的数字，就是不断起飞。

senses.title: Likely to change suddenly
senses.definition: of a situation or condition, liable to change quickly and dangerously
senses.definitionCN: 指局势或状况可能迅速而危险地变化
senses.example: The region's politics remain volatile after the election.
senses.exampleCN: 选举之后，该地区的政治局势仍不稳定。
senses.why: The flying image applies to a whole order, not just a price: what will not stay put can also break apart.
senses.whyCN: 「飞」的意象适用于整个秩序，而非单一价格：不肯停在原位的，也可能四分五裂。

senses.title: Quick to anger
senses.definition: of a person or temper, becoming angry suddenly and without much warning
senses.definitionCN: 指人或脾气突然发火，且少有预警
senses.example: His volatile temper made the meeting difficult.
senses.exampleCN: 他暴躁的脾气让会议很难进行。
senses.why: A temper is weather inside a person, and the same refusal to settle now describes a mood.
senses.whyCN: 脾气是一个人内心的天气，同一种「不肯安定」如今用来描述情绪。

senses.title: Lasting only a short time
senses.definition: of fame, memory or a condition, passing away quickly
senses.definitionCN: 指名声、记忆或状态很快消逝
senses.example: The band enjoyed volatile fame in the early years.
senses.exampleCN: 这支乐队早年的名声来得快去得也快。
senses.why: Fame flies past, so the literal flight becomes a statement about how long something lasts.
senses.whyCN: 名声会飞逝，于是字面的「飞行」变成对事物持续多久的陈述。

senses.title: Dangerously reactive
senses.definition: of a substance or mixture, able to react, ignite or explode easily
senses.definitionCN: 指物质或混合物容易反应、着火或爆炸
senses.example: The warehouse stored volatile chemicals away from any flame.
senses.exampleCN: 仓库把易反应的化学品存放在远离火源的地方。
senses.why: Reactive substances take off as heat and gas, which is the flying image made dangerous.
senses.whyCN: 反应性物质会以热与气体的形式腾起，这就是「飞」的意象变得危险。

senses.title: Wavering in data or results
senses.definition: of measurements or performance, varying widely from one reading to the next
senses.definitionCN: 指测量值或表现各次之间差异很大
senses.example: The sensor gave volatile readings during the storm.
senses.exampleCN: 风暴期间传感器读数起伏不定。
senses.why: A reading that jumps like a flying thing cannot be trusted as a measurement.
senses.whyCN: 像飞物一样跳动的读数，无法作为可靠的测量值。

senses.title: Not durable in alliance
senses.definition: of a partnership or agreement, likely to break or shift soon
senses.definitionCN: 指伙伴关系或协议可能很快破裂或改变
senses.example: The two parties formed a volatile alliance that lasted one season.
senses.exampleCN: 两方结成了一个只维持一季的脆弱联盟。
senses.why: An alliance that keeps shifting has no stable ground to stand on.
senses.whyCN: 不断变动的联盟，没有稳定地面可以站立。

senses.title: Lost when power is cut
senses.definition: of computer memory, holding data only while power is supplied
senses.definitionCN: 指计算机存储器只在供电时保存数据
senses.example: The device keeps the log in volatile memory until it is saved.
senses.exampleCN: 该设备把日志保存在易失性存储器中，直到被写入。
senses.why: Memory contents fly away when the power stops, so the technical name keeps the literal flight.
senses.whyCN: 断电时存储内容会飞走，因此这个技术名称保留了字面的「飞行」。

intro.en: Volatile comes from a Latin adjective for flying: the same word covers vapour that flies off, prices that will not settle, a temper that flares and memory that vanishes.
intro.cn: 这个词来自拉丁语表示「会飞的」形容词：同一个词覆盖飞走的蒸气、不肯落定的价格、突然爆发的脾气，以及会消失的记忆。

items.en: volare meant to fly, to move through the air.
items.cn: volare 意为「飞、在空中移动」。

items.en: volatilis described what flies or passes quickly, including birds and fleeting things.
items.cn: volatilis 描述会飞或迅速消逝的东西，包括鸟与短暂之物。

items.en: English adopted the adjective in the sixteenth century with the sense of flying or fleeting; the exact first date is approximate but the root is clear.
items.cn: 英语在十六世纪借入这个形容词，意为「飞行的、短暂的」；具体首见年份为约数，但词根清楚。

items.en: Chemistry made the flying literal: a volatile liquid is one that takes off as vapour.
items.cn: 化学让「飞」变得字面化：挥发性液体就是会以蒸气形式飞走的液体。

items.en: Finance and politics extended the image to prices and situations that will not stay put.
items.cn: 金融与政治把这个意象扩展到不肯停在原位的价格与局势。

items.en: Computing named memory volatile because its contents fly away when the power stops.
items.cn: 计算机领域把存储器称为易失的，因为断电时其内容会飞走。

note.en: The first group shares the flying root or looks close; the second group names nearby kinds of instability, and the note separates them from mere energy.
note.cn: 第一组共享「飞」的词根或形音相近；第二组是邻近的不稳定类说法，说明中把它们与单纯的「精力旺盛」分开。

entries.definition: The noun for the tendency to evaporate or to change sharply.
entries.definitionCN: 指易挥发或剧烈变化的性质。

entries.definition: The verb meaning to make a substance evaporate or to become vapour.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，指使物质挥发或变成蒸气。

entries.definition: Not evaporating easily, or, in computing, keeping data when power is off.
entries.definitionCN: 指不易挥发，或在计算机中断电仍保存数据。

entries.definition: The adjective itself, used in chemistry, finance, politics and computing.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词本身，用于化学、金融、政治与计算领域。

entries.definition: Able to turn to many uses; it looks close but its root is turning, not flying.
entries.definitionCN: 指能转向多种用途；形近，但词根是「转动」，不是「飞」。

entries.definition: Likely to change, fall or fail; broader and plainer than volatile.
entries.definitionCN: 指可能变化、倒下或失败；比本词更宽泛、更朴素。

entries.definition: Impossible to forecast; it stresses the lack of warning rather than the size of the swing.
entries.definitionCN: 指无法预测；强调缺乏预警，而非波动幅度。

entries.definition: Able to blow up, or a temper that erupts violently; it stresses the burst itself.
entries.definitionCN: 指会爆炸，或脾气猛烈爆发；强调爆发本身。

entries.definition: Full of energy and force; it describes strength in action, not instability or evaporation.
entries.definitionCN: 指精力充沛、有力；描述行动中的力量，而非不稳定或挥发。

entries.definition: Passing quickly; it covers the short-lived sense without the chemistry or finance ones.
entries.definitionCN: 指迅速消逝；只覆盖「短暂」这一义，不含化学与金融义。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations use the real Latin flying root, the real chemistry and finance phrases, and the real contrast with vigorous.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想使用真实的拉丁「飞」词根、真实的化学与金融搭配，以及与 vigorous 的真实区别。

normal.en: The root means fly: a volatile liquid flies into the air, and volatile prices fly up and down.
normal.cn: 词根意为「飞」：易挥发的液体飞进空气，易波动的价格上下飞。

normal.en: Volatile compound, volatile market and volatile memory are three real phrases from three fields.
normal.cn: 挥发性化合物、动荡的市场与易失性存储器是来自三个领域的真实搭配。

normal.en: The same word covers a solvent, a temper and a share price because all refuse to stay put.
normal.cn: 同一个词覆盖溶剂、脾气与股价，因为它们都不肯停在原地。

normal.en: Volatility is the noun; volatilize is the verb that sends a substance into vapour.
normal.cn: volatility 是名词；volatilize 是把物质送进蒸气的动词。

normal.en: Versatile is about turning, volatile is about flying; one changes uses, the other changes state.
normal.cn: versatile 说的是「转」，volatile 说的是「飞」；一个换用途，一个换状态。

abstract.en: What flies cannot be held; volatility is a warning that the present reading is not a promise.
abstract.cn: 会飞的东西握不住；波动性是一个警告：此刻的读数不是承诺。

abstract.en: A volatile temper and a volatile market share one structure: energy with no container.
abstract.cn: 暴躁的脾气与动荡的市场共享一个结构：没有容器的能量。

abstract.en: The word describes disappearance as well as change, which is why memory and fame are called volatile.
abstract.cn: 这个词既描述变化，也描述消失，所以记忆与名声也被称为短暂易逝。

examples.en: The lab stores volatile solvents in a cool cabinet away from heat.
examples.cn: 实验室把易挥发溶剂存放在远离热源的阴凉柜里。

examples.en: Currency markets grew volatile after the announcement.
examples.cn: 公告发布后，货币市场变得动荡。

examples.en: The old photographs are fading because the dyes are volatile.
examples.cn: 这些老照片正在褪色，因为染料不稳定。

dict_mnemonic.text: 读作「佛勒泰尔」——拉丁语「会飞的」：说走就走

root: 来自拉丁语 volatilis「会飞的、短暂的」← volare「飞」，经法语进入英语，十六世纪起用；化学义让「飞」字面化，金融与计算义再作延伸。词根清楚，首见年份为约数。

sensesIntro.en: Nine senses run from an evaporating liquid through prices, politics, temper, fame, reactive chemicals, readings, alliances and computer memory.
sensesIntro.cn: 九个义项从挥发的液体，经过价格、政治、脾气、名声、反应性化学品、读数、联盟，最后到计算机存储器。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: liquid in an open beaker keeps disappearing upward while a price curve jumps on the screen.
core.cn: 核心意象：敞口烧杯里的液体不断向上消失，屏幕上的价格曲线同时剧烈跳动。

branches.en: THE SUBSTANCE: a liquid that evaporates or a chemical that reacts dangerously.
branches.cn: 物质：会蒸发的液体，或会危险反应的化学品。

branches.en: THE NUMBERS: prices and readings that will not settle.
branches.cn: 数字：不肯落定的价格与读数。

branches.en: THE SITUATION: a political order or alliance likely to break.
branches.cn: 局势：可能破裂的政治秩序或联盟。

branches.en: THE TEMPER: anger that flares without warning.
branches.cn: 脾气：无预警爆发的怒火。

branches.en: THE VANISHING: fame and memory that pass, and data lost with the power.
branches.cn: 消失：消逝的名声与记忆，以及随断电丢失的数据。

intro.en: Volatile is a Latin flying stem with an adjective ending; chemistry, finance and computing keep adding noun and verb forms around it.
intro.cn: 这个词是拉丁「飞」词干加形容词词尾；化学、金融与计算不断在它周围添名词与动词形式。

latinIntro.en: Latin supplies volare, volatilis and volatilitas; English builds volatility, volatilize and nonvolatile on the same stem.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语提供了 volare、volatilis 与 volatilitas；英语在同一词干上构成 volatility、volatilize 与 nonvolatile。

items.example: The root supplies the flight.
items.exampleCN: 词根提供飞行。

items.example: The adjective adds the quality.
items.exampleCN: 形容词加上性质。

items.example: It marks the tendency.
items.exampleCN: 它标记倾向。

items.example: The borrowed word keeps the flight.
items.exampleCN: 借入的词保留飞行。

items.example: The Latin noun names the quality.
items.exampleCN: 拉丁名词命名这种性质。

items.example: It forms volatility.
items.exampleCN: 它构成 volatility。

items.example: It forms volatilize, to send into vapour.
items.exampleCN: 它构成 volatilize，即使之挥发。

items.example: It forms volatilization.
items.exampleCN: 它构成 volatilization。

items.example: It forms nonvolatile, the settled case.
items.exampleCN: 它构成 nonvolatile，即安定的情形。

derivatives.zh: 由形容词加性质名词词尾构成，义为「挥发性；波动性」
由形容词加使动词尾构成，义为「使挥发」
由挥发动词加动作名词词尾构成，义为「挥发过程」
由否定前缀加本词构成，义为「不挥发的」

definition_zh: 精力充沛的；强健有力的；有力的；旺盛的；积极的
definition_en: full of physical or mental force, and expressed with strength, energy and determination
core_image: 清晨的跑道上，一个人大步快跑，呼吸深沉，脚下的影子被拉得很长
scene: 清晨的跑道上，一位老人做完热身就开始快跑，呼吸深沉，脚步落地有声。She kept up a vigorous pace for the whole hour.
sceneCN: 这里指动作强健有力、节奏不慢（第 2 个义项：动作强健有力）；句意为她整整一小时都保持着有力的步速。图中可辨识物件：跑道、跑动的人、拉长的影子、腕上的计时表。

pos.zh: 精力充沛的；强健有力的；有力的

derivatives.zh: 同一词根的名词，义为「精力；活力」
由形容词加副词词尾构成，义为「有力地；大力地」
由表示「使」的前缀加名词再加动词词尾构成，义为「使充满活力」
由动词加现在分词词尾构成，义为「令人精神焕发的」
由动词加动作名词词尾构成，义为「焕发活力」

senses.title: Full of bodily energy
senses.definition: of a person, strong, active and full of stamina
senses.definitionCN: 指人强壮、活跃、耐力充足
senses.example: A vigorous hiker reached the ridge before noon.
senses.exampleCN: 一位精力充沛的徒步者中午前就到了山脊。
senses.why: The Latin root means to be lively and to flourish; the adjective first describes a living body in full force.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁词根意为「有生气、兴旺」；这个形容词最初描述全力运转的活体。

senses.title: Strong in movement
senses.definition: of an action or pace, carried out with force and energy
senses.definitionCN: 指动作或步速以力量与能量完成
senses.example: She kept up a vigorous pace for the whole hour.
senses.exampleCN: 她整整一小时都保持着有力的步速。
senses.why: The image of flourishing applies to movement: a body that moves with force is a body in full life.
senses.whyCN: 「兴旺」的意象适用于运动：有力移动的身体就是处于全盛生命状态的身体。

senses.title: Forceful in growth
senses.definition: of growth or change, strong and rapid rather than weak
senses.definitionCN: 指增长或变化强劲迅速，而非疲弱
senses.example: The seedlings showed vigorous growth after the rain.
senses.exampleCN: 雨后幼苗呈现出旺盛的生长。
senses.why: Plants flourish visibly, so the root's sense of thriving passes straight into the language of growth.
senses.whyCN: 植物会明显地兴旺，因此词根的「兴旺」直接进入生长的话语。

senses.title: Assertive in effort or support
senses.titleCN: 努力与支持上的积极有力
senses.definition: of effort or advocacy, energetic and determined
senses.definitionCN: 指努力或主张充满能量与决心
senses.example: The group mounted a vigorous campaign against the closure.
senses.exampleCN: 该团体发起了一场声势浩大的反对关闭运动。
senses.why: Advocacy is energy directed at a public goal, which is flourishing turned outward.
senses.whyCN: 主张是把能量指向一个公共目标，也就是向外转的「兴旺」。

senses.title: Robust in health
senses.definition: of an organism or plant, healthy and resistant
senses.definitionCN: 指生物或植物健康且有抵抗力
senses.example: The old tree is still vigorous after a dry summer.
senses.exampleCN: 经过一个干旱的夏天，这棵老树仍然旺盛。
senses.why: Health is the body's own flourishing, so an organism that resists hardship is called vigorous.
senses.whyCN: 健康就是身体自身的兴旺，因此能抗住艰难的生物被称为旺盛。

senses.title: Active in body systems
senses.definition: of a bodily process, working strongly and efficiently
senses.definitionCN: 指身体过程运转有力而有效
senses.example: Vigorous circulation helped the wound heal quickly.
senses.exampleCN: 旺盛的血液循环帮助伤口很快愈合。
senses.why: Internal processes are the body's engine, and strong flow is flourishing inside the frame.
senses.whyCN: 体内过程是身体的引擎，强劲的流动就是骨架内部的兴旺。

senses.title: Heated in debate or competition
senses.definition: of discussion or contest, conducted with force and intensity
senses.definitionCN: 指讨论或竞赛以力量与强度进行
senses.example: A vigorous debate followed the proposal.
senses.exampleCN: 提案之后展开了一场激烈的辩论。
senses.why: Debate is mental force made audible, so the adjective moves from muscle to argument.
senses.whyCN: 辩论是能被听见的心智力量，于是这个形容词从肌肉移到了论证。

senses.title: Strong in enforcement
senses.definition: of action by an authority, firm and thorough
senses.definitionCN: 指权威机构的行为坚决而彻底
senses.example: The agency promised vigorous enforcement of the new rules.
senses.exampleCN: 该机构承诺有力执行新规。
senses.why: Enforcement applies force to a rule, which is the same energy aimed at an institution.
senses.whyCN: 执法把力量施加于规则，也就是同一股能量指向制度。

senses.title: Forceful in style
senses.definition: of writing, speech or art, bold and energetic in expression
senses.definitionCN: 指写作、言辞或艺术表达大胆而有力
senses.example: The novel's vigorous prose keeps the reader awake.
senses.exampleCN: 这部小说雄健的文笔让读者保持清醒。
senses.why: Style is force made visible in words, the last place where a body's vigor can show.
senses.whyCN: 风格是力量在文字中变得可见，也是身体的活力最后能显现的地方。

intro.en: Vigorous comes from a Latin verb meaning to be lively and to flourish; the noun vigor was in English before the adjective, and both keep the image of a body in full force.
intro.cn: 这个词来自拉丁语表示「有生气、兴旺」的动词；名词 vigor 先进入英语，形容词随后而来，两者都保留「全力运转的身体」这一意象。

items.en: vigere meant to be lively, to flourish, to be in full strength.
items.cn: vigere 意为「有生气、兴旺、处于全力状态」。

items.en: The noun vigor named the force itself, the active strength of a living thing.
items.cn: 名词 vigor 命名那股力量本身，即活物的活跃强度。

items.en: The adjective vigorosus described something full of that force.
items.cn: 形容词 vigorosus 描述充满这股力量的事物。

items.en: French carried the adjective to English in the fourteenth century; the first date is approximate but the stem is clear.
items.cn: 法语在十四世纪把这个形容词带到英语；首见年份为约数，但词干清楚。

items.en: English first applied it to bodies and actions, then to growth, argument and style.
items.cn: 英语先把它用于身体与动作，再扩展到生长、论证与文风。

items.en: Modern usage speaks of vigorous campaigns, enforcement and debate, where force is applied to a public task.
items.cn: 现代用法会说声势浩大的运动、有力执行与激烈辩论，这里的力量被用于公共任务。

note.en: The first group shares the vigor stem or looks close; the second group names nearby kinds of strength, and the note separates vigor from volatility.
note.cn: 第一组共享 vigor 词干或形音相近；第二组是邻近的力量类说法，说明中把「精力旺盛」与「易变」分开。

entries.definition: The noun for active strength of body or mind.
entries.definitionCN: 指身体或心智的活跃力量。

entries.definition: The adverb for acting with force and energy.
entries.definitionCN: 副词，指以力量与能量行动。

entries.definition: To fill someone or something with new energy.
entries.definitionCN: 指给某人或某物注入新的活力。

entries.definition: Describing something that refreshes and strengthens.
entries.definitionCN: 形容令人振奋、强身的东西。

entries.definition: Strict and thorough; it looks close but its root means stiff, not lively.
entries.definitionCN: 指严格彻底的；形近，但词根意为「僵硬」，而非「有生气」。

entries.definition: Watchful; it shares some sound but comes from a root meaning to watch.
entries.definitionCN: 指警惕的；读音部分相近，但词根意为「守望」。

entries.definition: Full of energy and activity; the most general word for liveliness.
entries.definitionCN: 指精力充沛、活跃；是表示「有活力」最通用的词。

entries.definition: Strong, healthy and hard to damage; it stresses resilience more than drive.
entries.definitionCN: 指强壮、健康、不易受损；强调抗压，而非冲劲。

entries.definition: Strong in effect or expression; it stresses impact on others.
entries.definitionCN: 指效果或表达上有力；强调对他人的冲击。

entries.definition: Changing sharply and unpredictably; it shares an -ile shape but names instability, not strength.
entries.definitionCN: 指剧烈而不可预测地变化；共享 -ile 外形，但说的是不稳定，不是力量。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations use the real Latin flourish root, the real body-and-growth pairs, and the real contrast with volatile.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想使用真实的拉丁「兴旺」词根、真实的身体与生长搭配，以及与 volatile 的真实区别。

normal.en: The root means flourish: a vigorous person is a plant in full growth and a body in full motion.
normal.cn: 词根意为「兴旺」：精力充沛的人既是全力生长的植物，也是全力运动的身体。

normal.en: Vigorous exercise, vigorous growth and vigorous debate are three real phrases.
normal.cn: 剧烈运动、旺盛生长与激烈辩论是三个真实搭配。

normal.en: Vigor is the noun, vigorously is the adverb, invigorate is the verb that adds energy.
normal.cn: vigor 是名词，vigorously 是副词，invigorate 是注入能量的动词。

normal.en: Rigorous looks close but means strict; do not let the two -ous endings swap places.
normal.cn: rigorous 形近但意为严格；别让两个 -ous 词尾互换位置。

normal.en: Volatile is about flying away; vigorous is about pushing forward.
normal.cn: volatile 说的是飞走；vigorous 说的是向前推进。

abstract.en: Vigor is force that renews itself; a single burst of energy is not the same as sustained strength.
abstract.cn: 活力是能自我更新的力量；一次爆发不同于持续的力量。

abstract.en: The same adjective can praise a body, a plant, an argument or a law, because all need force to hold their shape.
abstract.cn: 同一个形容词可赞身体、植物、论证或法律，因为它们都需要力量来维持形状。

abstract.en: Vigorous action without direction is merely noisy; the word describes force, not wisdom.
abstract.cn: 没有方向的强力行动只是喧闹；这个词描述力量，而非智慧。

examples.en: Doctors recommend thirty minutes of vigorous activity several times a week.
examples.cn: 医生建议每周进行几次三十分钟的剧烈活动。

examples.en: The young vines are vigorous and need pruning every season.
examples.cn: 这些幼藤长势旺盛，每季都需要修剪。

examples.en: The senator mounted a vigorous defense of the treaty.
examples.cn: 这位参议员为条约作了有力的辩护。

dict_mnemonic.text: 读作「维格若斯」——像植物一样「正当旺」，浑身是劲

root: 来自拉丁语 vigorosus「充满活力的」← vigor「活力、力量」← vigere「有生气、兴旺」；经法语于十四世纪进入英语。词源链清楚，首见年份为约数。

sensesIntro.en: Nine senses run from a strong body and strong movement through growth, effort, health, circulation, debate, enforcement and style.
sensesIntro.cn: 九个义项从强壮的身体与有力的动作，经过生长、努力、健康、循环、辩论、执法，最后到文风。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a runner holds a long, strong stride, breathing deep, shadow stretched behind.
core.cn: 核心意象：跑者保持又长又有力的步伐，呼吸深沉，影子被拉在身后。

branches.en: THE BODY AND THE PLANT: a person or organism in full health.
branches.cn: 身体与植物：处于完全健康状态的人或生物。

branches.en: THE MOTION INSIDE: strong pace and vigorous circulation.
branches.cn: 体内的运动：有力的步速与旺盛的循环。

branches.en: THE RISING CURVE: growth that is rapid and healthy.
branches.cn: 上升的曲线：迅速而健康的生长。

branches.en: THE PUBLIC PUSH: campaigns, debates and enforcement carried out with force.
branches.cn: 公共推力：以力量开展的运动、辩论与执法。

branches.en: THE BOLD PAGE: prose or art that moves with energy.
branches.cn: 雄健的书页：充满能量地推进的文字或艺术。

intro.en: Vigorous is a Latin stem for flourishing plus an adjective ending, with a noun and a verb built around it.
intro.cn: 这个词是拉丁「兴旺」词干加形容词词尾，周围还有名词与动词形式。

latinIntro.en: Latin supplies vigere, vigor and vigorosus; English adds vigorously, invigorate and invigoration.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语提供了 vigere、vigor 与 vigorosus；英语再加 vigorously、invigorate 与 invigoration。

items.example: The root supplies the living force.
items.exampleCN: 词根提供生命的力量。

items.example: The noun names the force itself.
items.exampleCN: 名词命名力量本身。

items.example: The adjective adds fullness.
items.exampleCN: 形容词加上「充满」。

items.example: It forms the English adjective.
items.exampleCN: 它构成英语形容词。

items.example: The borrowed adjective keeps the body image.
items.exampleCN: 借入的形容词保留身体意象。

items.example: The adverb adds manner.
items.exampleCN: 副词加上方式。

items.example: It turns vigor into a verb of giving.
items.exampleCN: 它把 vigor 变成「给予」的动词。

items.example: It forms invigorate, to give energy.
items.exampleCN: 它构成 invigorate，即使之充满活力。

items.example: It forms invigoration.
items.exampleCN: 它构成 invigoration。

derivatives.zh: 同词根名词，义为「活力」
由形容词加副词词尾构成，义为「有力地」
由使动词缀构成，义为「使充满活力」
由现在分词构成，义为「令人振奋的」
由动作名词词尾构成，义为「焕发活力」

definition_zh: 表面的；表层的；肤浅的；不深入的；浅表的
definition_en: belonging only to the surface, or dealing with something quickly and without depth
core_image: 检查员绕着房子外墙走一圈，只看新刷的漆，屋里的裂管被墙挡住
scene: 检查员只绕着外墙走了一圈，看了看新刷的漆，就在表格上打了勾，没有打开任何一个房间。The inspection was superficial and missed the cracked pipes.
sceneCN: 这里指检查只看表面、不深入内部（第 4 个义项：不深入的调查）；句意为这次检查流于表面，漏掉了裂开的管道。图中可辨识物件：房屋外墙、新漆、打勾的表格、被墙挡住的管道。

pos.zh: 表面的；肤浅的；不深入的

derivatives.zh: 由形容词加副词词尾构成，义为「表面上；肤浅地」
由形容词加表示性质的名词词尾构成，义为「肤浅；表面性」
由形容词加表示性质的名词词尾构成，义为「表面的性质」，较少使用

senses.title: Belonging to the physical surface
senses.definition: located at or affecting only the outer layer of an object or body
senses.definitionCN: 位于或只影响物体或身体的外层
senses.example: The cut was superficial and needed only a bandage.
senses.exampleCN: 这道切口很浅，只需包扎。
senses.why: The Latin noun for surface supplies the literal sense: the adjective describes what sits on the face of a thing.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语表示「表面」的名词提供了字面义：这个形容词描述位于事物表层的东西。

senses.title: Knowledge without depth
senses.definition: of knowledge or understanding, broad in appearance but lacking detail or real grasp
senses.definitionCN: 指知识或理解看似广博，却缺少细节与真正掌握
senses.example: His knowledge of the language is superficial.
senses.exampleCN: 他对这门语言的知识很肤浅。
senses.why: The surface image moves inward: a mind can also stay on the top layer.
senses.whyCN: 表面意象转向内部：心智也可以停留在最上层。

senses.title: Judging by appearance
senses.definition: of a judgment or person, based on looks rather than substance
senses.definitionCN: 指判断或人依据外貌而非实质
senses.example: The critics were superficial and never read the whole report.
senses.exampleCN: 批评者只看表面，从未读完整个报告。
senses.why: When the face is all that is consulted, the word becomes a moral criticism.
senses.whyCN: 当只参考那张「脸」时，这个词就变成一种道德批评。

senses.title: An inquiry that stays on the outside
senses.definition: of an examination or analysis, quick and incomplete, missing what lies beneath
senses.definitionCN: 指检查或分析迅速而不完整，漏掉藏在下面的东西
senses.example: The inspection was superficial and missed the cracked pipes.
senses.exampleCN: 这次检查流于表面，漏掉了裂开的管道。
senses.why: The inspector's route never left the surface, which is the literal geometry of the word.
senses.whyCN: 检查员的路线从未离开表面，这正是这个词字面上的几何关系。

senses.title: Apparent but not real
senses.titleCN: 表面上如此而实际不然
senses.definition: of a similarity, calm or peace, true only at the visible level
senses.definitionCN: 指相似、平静或和平只在可见层面成立
senses.example: There is a superficial resemblance between the two designs.
senses.exampleCN: 这两个设计之间存在表面的相似。
senses.why: A resemblance that exists only at the visible face is a surface match and nothing more.
senses.whyCN: 只在可见表面成立的相似，只是表面相符，别无所指。

senses.title: Affecting only the skin
senses.definition: of an injury or condition, limited to the outer tissue
senses.definitionCN: 指损伤或病变限于外层组织
senses.example: The burn was superficial and healed within a week.
senses.exampleCN: 烧伤很浅，一周内就愈合了。
senses.why: Medicine keeps the oldest physical sense: the injury touches only the outer layer.
senses.whyCN: 医学保留了最古老的物理义：损伤只触及外层。

senses.title: Decorative rather than structural
senses.definition: of a change or feature, improving appearance without altering function
senses.definitionCN: 指改变或特征改善外观，却不改变功能
senses.example: The renovation was superficial and left the wiring untouched.
senses.exampleCN: 这次翻新只做了表面，线路原封未动。
senses.why: A renovation that changes appearance but not function repeats the same surface-only image.
senses.whyCN: 只改外观不改功能的翻新，重复了同一幅「只动表面」的图景。

senses.title: A quick, cursory reading
senses.definition: of reading or study, done quickly without close attention
senses.definitionCN: 指阅读或学习快速而不仔细
senses.example: A superficial reading misses the argument's contradictions.
senses.exampleCN: 粗读会漏掉论证中的矛盾。
senses.why: Reading quickly means touching the page but never the argument beneath it.
senses.whyCN: 快速阅读意味着只碰到纸面，却从不进入下面的论证。

senses.title: Shallow in feeling or interest
senses.definition: of emotion or interest, easily formed and easily dropped
senses.definitionCN: 指情感或兴趣容易形成，也容易放弃
senses.example: Their enthusiasm proved superficial once the work began.
senses.exampleCN: 工作一开始，他们的热情就显得浅薄。
senses.why: Emotion that forms and fades easily stays on the surface of a person.
senses.whyCN: 来得容易去得也容易的情感，只停留在一个人的表面。

intro.en: Superficial is built from Latin words for above and for face: what belongs to the top face of a thing, and by extension what never goes below it.
intro.cn: 这个词由拉丁语表示「在上」与「脸面」的词构成：属于事物最上面那层的，引申为从不往下的。

items.en: facies meant form, face, outward appearance.
items.cn: facies 意为「形状、脸面、外表」。

items.en: super- meant above or over, and it places one thing on top of another.
items.cn: super- 意为「在上、超过」，把一物置于另一物之上。

items.en: superficies named the surface, literally the upper face of a body.
items.cn: superficies 命名表面，字面就是物体上面的那张「脸」。

items.en: The adjective superficialis described whatever belongs to that upper face.
items.cn: 形容词 superficialis 描述属于那层上表面的一切。

items.en: English took the adjective through French in the fifteenth century; the first date is approximate but the Latin line is clear.
items.cn: 英语在十五世纪经法语借入这个形容词；首见年份为约数，但拉丁来源线索清楚。

items.en: Medicine kept the literal skin sense, while criticism turned the same word into a judgment about depth.
items.cn: 医学保留了字面的皮肤义，批评则把同一个词变成关于深度的判断。

note.en: The first group shares the surface root or looks close; the second group names nearby ideas of shallowness, and the note places sophisticated at the opposite pole.
note.cn: 第一组共享「表面」词根或形音相近；第二组是邻近的浅薄类说法，说明中把 sophisticated 放在相反一极。

entries.definition: The adverb for looking only at the surface or doing something without depth.
entries.definitionCN: 副词，指只看表面或不深入地做事。

entries.definition: The noun for the quality of staying on the surface.
entries.definitionCN: 指停留在表面的性质。

entries.definition: A technical term for surface or extent, still used in law and geometry.
entries.definitionCN: 指表面或面积的技术术语，仍用于法律与几何。

entries.definition: More than is needed; it looks close but its root means to flow, not a face.
entries.definitionCN: 指多余过剩；形近，但词根意为「流动」，而非「脸面」。

entries.definition: The outer layer of a thing; the everyday noun behind the adjective.
entries.definitionCN: 指事物的外层；是这个形容词背后的日常名词。

entries.definition: Not deep, literally or mentally; it is plainer and often more judgmental about people.
entries.definitionCN: 指不深，字面或心智皆可；更朴素，用于人时判断更强。

entries.definition: Done quickly and without care; it stresses speed rather than surface location.
entries.definitionCN: 指快速而不经心；强调速度，而非处在表面。

entries.definition: Only as deep as the skin; a vivid idiom for beauty or feeling that does not last.
entries.definitionCN: 指只深及皮肤；形容美貌或感情不持久的一个生动习语。

entries.definition: Complex, refined and deeply informed; it is the near opposite of superficial in judgments of knowledge or taste.
entries.definitionCN: 指复杂、精细、见识深；在评价知识或品味时，几乎是本词的反面。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations use the real above-the-face image, the real medicine and criticism split, and the real contrast with sophisticated.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想使用真实的「在上之脸」意象、真实的医学与批评分流，以及与 sophisticated 的真实对照。

normal.en: super means above and facies means face: superficial is what lies on the face of things.
normal.cn: super 是「在上」，facies 是「脸」：superficial 就是躺在事物脸上的东西。

normal.en: A superficial wound touches the skin; a superficial reading touches the page and nothing under it.
normal.cn: 浅表伤口只碰皮肤；粗读只碰纸面，碰不到纸下的东西。

normal.en: Superficial knowledge, superficial resemblance and superficial calm are three real phrases.
normal.cn: 肤浅的知识、表面的相似与表面上的平静是三个真实搭配。

normal.en: The noun superficiality is the quality; the adverb superficially is the manner.
normal.cn: 名词 superficiality 是性质，副词 superficially 是方式。

normal.en: Sophisticated is its opposite pole: depth, refinement and complexity against surface and speed.
normal.cn: sophisticated 是相反一极：深度、精细与复杂，对抗表面与仓促。

abstract.en: A surface is real, but it is also the thinnest part of anything.
abstract.cn: 表面是真实的，但也是任何事物最薄的一层。

abstract.en: Superficial judgments are cheap because they cost no time; that is exactly why they are dangerous.
abstract.cn: 肤浅的判断很廉价，因为不花时间；这恰恰是它危险的原因。

abstract.en: The same word praises a shallow wound and condemns a shallow mind, though the depth is measured differently.
abstract.cn: 同一个词既赞浅表伤口，也贬浅薄心智，只是「深度」的度量方式不同。

examples.en: The report offers a superficial survey but no real explanation.
examples.cn: 这份报告只做了表面综述，没有真正的解释。

examples.en: They share a superficial resemblance, though their mechanisms are entirely different.
examples.cn: 它们有表面的相似，但机制完全不同。

examples.en: The nurse cleaned the superficial cut and sent the patient home.
examples.cn: 护士清理了浅表的伤口，就让病人回家了。

dict_mnemonic.text: 读作「苏珀菲舍尔」——只停在「上面那张脸」，不进里面

root: 来自拉丁语 superficialis「表面的」← superficies「表面」← super-「在上」+ facies「脸面、外形」，经法语于十五世纪进入英语。词源链清楚，首见年份为约数。

sensesIntro.en: Nine senses run from a shallow wound through knowledge and judgment, inquiry, appearance, skin, decoration, quick reading and shallow feeling.
sensesIntro.cn: 九个义项从浅表伤口，经过知识、判断、调查、外观、皮肤、装饰、粗读，最后到浅薄的情感。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: an inspector walks once around a house, looks at fresh paint and never opens a door.
core.cn: 核心意象：检查员绕房子走一圈，看了看新漆，却一扇门也没打开。

branches.en: THE OUTER LAYER: a shallow wound and a change that only alters appearance.
branches.cn: 外层：浅表伤口，以及只改外观的改变。

branches.en: THE QUICK GRASP: knowledge and reading that stop at the first layer.
branches.cn: 快速把握：停在第一层的知识与阅读。

branches.en: THE UNCAREFUL JUDGMENT: a critic or inspector who never goes inside.
branches.cn: 草率判断：从不进去的批评者或检查员。

branches.en: THE APPARENT MATCH: a resemblance or calm that holds only on the surface.
branches.cn: 表面相符：只在表层成立的相似或平静。

branches.en: THE THIN FEELING: enthusiasm that forms and fades easily.
branches.cn: 薄薄的情感：来得容易、去得也容易的热情。

intro.en: Superficial is a prefix meaning above, a root meaning face, and an adjective ending of belonging.
intro.cn: 这个词是一个表示「在上」的前缀、一个表示「脸面」的词根，加一个表示「属于」的形容词词尾。

latinIntro.en: Latin supplies facies, superficies and superficialis; French carries the adjective into English.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语提供了 facies、superficies 与 superficialis；法语把这个形容词带进英语。

items.example: It places the layer on top.
items.exampleCN: 它把那一层放在上面。

items.example: The root names the visible face.
items.exampleCN: 词根命名可见的脸面。

items.example: Prefix and root name the upper face.
items.exampleCN: 前缀与词根命名上表面。

items.example: The adjective adds belonging.
items.exampleCN: 形容词加上「属于」。

items.example: It forms the English adjective.
items.exampleCN: 它构成英语形容词。

items.example: The borrowed word keeps both senses.
items.exampleCN: 借入的词兼含两义。

items.example: It forms superficially.
items.exampleCN: 它构成 superficially。

items.example: It forms superficiality.
items.exampleCN: 它构成 superficiality。

items.example: The everyday noun keeps the face image.
items.exampleCN: 日常名词保留「脸面」意象。

derivatives.zh: 由形容词加副词词尾构成，义为「表面上」
由形容词加性质名词词尾构成，义为「肤浅」
由形容词加性质名词词尾构成，义为「表面性」

definition_zh: 复杂精密的；老练的；有品位的；精密的；世故的；高级的
definition_en: highly developed, complex and refined, or showing worldly experience and cultivated taste
core_image: 掌心大小的设备里叠着十几层电路，工程师用平板展开一张三维结构图
scene: 展厅中央摆着一台只有手掌大的设备，里面却叠着十几层电路，工程师用平板调出三维模型慢慢旋转。The new spectrometer is sophisticated enough to detect traces of a single element.
sceneCN: 这里指技术构造复杂而精密（第 1 个义项：复杂精密）；句意为这台新光谱仪精密得足以检测出单一元素的微量痕迹。图中可辨识物件：掌上设备、多层电路、平板上的三维模型、展台灯。

pos.zh: 复杂精密的；老练的；有品位的；世故的

derivatives.zh: 由形容词加表示状态的名词词尾构成，义为「精密；老练；品位」
同一词干构成的动词与名词，义为「使复杂精巧」与「老于世故的人」
由否定前缀加本词构成，义为「不复杂的；单纯质朴的」
由形容词加副词词尾构成，义为「精密地；老练地」，较少使用

senses.title: Complex and finely made
senses.definition: of a device, system or method, highly developed with many carefully arranged parts
senses.definitionCN: 指设备、系统或方法高度发展，由许多精心安排的部件组成
senses.example: The new spectrometer is sophisticated enough to detect traces of a single element.
senses.exampleCN: 这台新光谱仪精密得足以检测出单一元素的微量痕迹。
senses.why: The word began as a charge of adulteration and ended as praise of complexity, an inversion worth remembering.
senses.whyCN: 这个词起初指控「掺假」，最后却用来赞美复杂，这一反转值得记住。

senses.title: Worldly and experienced
senses.definition: of a person, experienced in social life and hard to deceive
senses.definitionCN: 指人在社会生活中经验丰富，不易受骗
senses.example: She is sophisticated enough to read the room before she speaks.
senses.exampleCN: 她足够老练，开口之前就能读懂现场气氛。
senses.why: Nineteenth-century English moved the word from mixtures to manners: experience became a kind of refinement.
senses.whyCN: 十九世纪英语把这个词从「混合物」转向「举止」：经验本身成了一种精致。

senses.title: Cultivated in taste
senses.definition: of taste or style, refined and informed rather than crude
senses.definitionCN: 指品味或风格精致有见识，而非粗陋
senses.example: The restaurant offers a sophisticated menu without any fuss.
senses.exampleCN: 这家餐厅提供精致而不张扬的菜单。
senses.why: Taste is the surface where experience becomes visible, so the two senses often appear together.
senses.whyCN: 品味是经验变得可见的表层，因此两种含义常一起出现。

senses.title: Precise in method
senses.definition: of a technique or instrument, accurate and technically advanced
senses.definitionCN: 指技术或仪器准确且技术先进
senses.example: The lab uses sophisticated methods to date the samples.
senses.exampleCN: 实验室用精密的方法为样本测定年代。
senses.why: A method with many carefully arranged steps is complex in the modern, approving sense of the word.
senses.whyCN: 步骤繁多且精心安排的方法，就是这个词现代褒义上的「复杂」。

senses.title: Adulterated, in the old sense
senses.definition: historically, mixed with a foreign substance so as to be impure
senses.definitionCN: 历史上指掺入外来物质而变得不纯
senses.example: The seventeenth-century label warned that the wine was sophisticated.
senses.exampleCN: 十七世纪的标签警告说这酒掺了假。
senses.why: This older sense survives mainly in dictionaries and explains why the modern praise sounds ironic at first.
senses.whyCN: 这个旧义主要留存于词典中，也解释了为何现代的赞美乍听有些反讽。

senses.title: Knowing in the ways of the world
senses.definition: of a view or attitude, shaped by broad experience rather than innocence
senses.definitionCN: 指看法或态度由广泛经验塑造，而非天真
senses.example: He gave a sophisticated account of how the deal was really made.
senses.exampleCN: 他就这笔交易的真实达成方式给出了老于世故的叙述。
senses.why: A view shaped by exposure to many dealings is worldly rather than innocent.
senses.whyCN: 由许多往来塑造的看法，是世故的，而非天真的。

senses.title: Advanced in the market
senses.definition: of a product or market, aimed at demanding and knowledgeable buyers
senses.definitionCN: 指产品或市场面向要求高、懂行的买家
senses.example: The brand moved into a more sophisticated segment last year.
senses.exampleCN: 该品牌去年进入了更高端的市场区间。
senses.why: Complex refinement is also a market position, aimed at buyers who can tell the difference.
senses.whyCN: 复杂的精致也是一种市场定位，面向那些分得出差别的买家。

senses.title: Subtle in reasoning or strategy
senses.definition: of an argument or plan, subtle and carefully constructed
senses.definitionCN: 指论证或计划细致而精心构造
senses.example: The paper offers a sophisticated defense of the policy.
senses.exampleCN: 这篇论文为该政策作了精妙的辩护。
senses.why: An argument with layered steps is complex in the mental sense, where refinement is subtlety.
senses.whyCN: 层层推进的论证在智识意义上是复杂的，在那里精致就是细微。

senses.title: Refined in daily life
senses.definition: of food, decor or habits, showing cultivated and complex preferences
senses.definitionCN: 指食物、陈设或习惯显示出有修养且复杂的偏好
senses.example: Their sophisticated dinner parties never feel formal.
senses.exampleCN: 他们的精致晚宴从不显得拘谨。
senses.why: Cultivated preferences in food and decor are complexity made visible in daily life.
senses.whyCN: 食物与陈设上经修养的偏好，是复杂在日常生活里变得可见。

intro.en: Sophisticated began with Greek wisdom, passed through the figure of the sophist and an old sense of adulteration, and only later became praise for complexity and refinement.
intro.cn: 这个词始于希腊语的「智慧」，经过「智者」这一身份与「掺假」的旧义，后来才变成对复杂与精致的赞美。

items.en: sophos meant wise, skilled, clever; it is the root of philosophy as well.
items.cn: sophos 意为「有智慧、有技艺、聪明」，也是 philosophy 的词根。

items.en: A sophistes was a skilled professional, later a paid teacher of argument, and the word acquired a suspicious tone.
items.cn: sophistes 原指有技艺的专业人士，后来指收费教授论辩的教师，这个词因此带上可疑色彩。

items.en: Latin took the Greek adjective as sophisticus, describing sophist argument and later dishonest mixture.
items.cn: 拉丁语借入希腊形容词作 sophisticus，描述诡辩，后来也指不老实的掺混。

items.en: The verb sophisticare meant to adulterate or tamper with something.
items.cn: 动词 sophisticare 意为「掺假、做手脚」。

items.en: English first used the participle for something adulterated; the first date is approximate but the Greek line is clear.
items.cn: 英语最初用这个分词指被掺假的东西；首见年份为约数，但希腊来源线索清楚。

items.en: By the nineteenth century the word had reversed: worldly experience and complex refinement became the praised qualities.
items.cn: 到十九世纪，这个词发生了反转：世故经验与复杂精致成了被赞美的品质。

note.en: The first group shares the sophos stem or looks close; the second group names nearby kinds of depth, and the note sets it against superficial.
note.cn: 第一组共享 sophos 词干或形音相近；第二组是邻近的深度类说法，说明中把它与 superficial 对照。

entries.definition: The noun for complexity, refinement or worldly knowledge.
entries.definitionCN: 指复杂、精致或世故的知识。

entries.definition: A worldly person, or the verb to make something more complex or refined.
entries.definitionCN: 指老于世故的人，或使某物更复杂精致的动词。

entries.definition: Simple and plain, sometimes in a good way and sometimes as a criticism.
entries.definitionCN: 指简单朴素，有时是褒义，有时是批评。

entries.definition: Relating to sophists or to clever but misleading argument.
entries.definitionCN: 指与智者派有关的，或指巧辩而误导的论证。

entries.definition: Pretentious and immature; it joins the wise root to a root for fool.
entries.definitionCN: 指自命不凡又幼稚；把「智慧」词根与「愚人」词根接在一起。

entries.definition: Purified and polished in taste or manners; it stresses the removal of what is coarse.
entries.definitionCN: 指品味或举止经提纯打磨；强调去掉粗陋。

entries.definition: Far along in development; it stresses technical progress, not social polish.
entries.definitionCN: 指发展程度高；强调技术进步，而非社交修养。

entries.definition: Developed through training and education, especially in a person's mind or taste.
entries.definitionCN: 指经由训练与教育发展而成，尤指心智或品味。

entries.definition: Experienced in practical affairs; it stresses exposure rather than refinement.
entries.definitionCN: 指在实际事务中有经验；强调阅历，而非精致。

entries.definition: Staying on the surface without depth; in judgments of knowledge or taste it is the opposite pole.
entries.definitionCN: 指停留在表面、没有深度；在评价知识与品味时是相反一极。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations use the real Greek wisdom root, the real inversion from adulteration to refinement, and the real contrast with superficial.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想使用真实的希腊「智慧」词根、真实的「掺假到精致」反转，以及与 superficial 的真实对照。

normal.en: Sophos means wise: sophisticated things and people carry a long history of skill and knowledge.
normal.cn: sophos 意为「智慧」：精致的事物与人身上带着悠久的技艺与知识史。

normal.en: The word once meant tampered with; remember the reversal and the modern praise will feel earned.
normal.cn: 这个词曾经意为「被做手脚」；记住这次反转，现代的赞美就显得有来历。

normal.en: Sophisticated technology, sophisticated audience and sophisticated design are three real phrases.
normal.cn: 精密技术、有见识的观众与精致的设计是三个真实搭配。

normal.en: Sophistication is the noun, unsophisticated is the plain opposite, and both keep the wisdom stem.
normal.cn: sophistication 是名词，unsophisticated 是朴素的反面，两者都保留「智慧」词干。

normal.en: Superficial stops at the face; sophisticated goes into the layers behind it.
normal.cn: superficial 停在脸面；sophisticated 走进脸面后面的层。

abstract.en: Complexity is not virtue by itself; a sophisticated lie is still a lie.
abstract.cn: 复杂本身不是美德；一个精密的谎言仍然是谎言。

abstract.en: The word's history warns that polish can be a form of tampering, and that the two meanings never fully separate.
abstract.cn: 这个词的历史提醒：打磨也可能是做手脚，两种含义从未完全分开。

abstract.en: Sophistication is what experience looks like when it has been shaped into taste.
abstract.cn: 精致是经验被塑造成品味之后的模样。

examples.en: The new hearing aid uses sophisticated software to separate speech from noise.
examples.cn: 这款新助听器用精密软件把语音与噪声分开。

examples.en: She moved through the reception with the ease of a sophisticated host.
examples.cn: 她以老练主人的从容穿梭在招待会上。

examples.en: The argument is sophisticated but rests on one unproven assumption.
examples.cn: 这个论证很精妙，却建立在一个未经证明的假设上。

dict_mnemonic.text: 读作「索菲斯提给提德」——从「智者」到「掺假」再到「精致」，一路翻转

root: 来自希腊语 sophos「智慧」→ sophistes「智者」→ sophistikos，经拉丁语 sophisticus 与中世纪拉丁语 sophisticare「掺假」构成分词，十七世纪英语先指「掺假的」，十九世纪转为「世故、精致」。来源链清楚，首见年份为约数。

sensesIntro.en: Nine senses run from complex machinery through worldly experience, taste, precise methods, the old adulterated sense, worldliness, high-end markets, subtle argument and refined living.
sensesIntro.cn: 九个义项从复杂机械，经过世故经验、品味、精密方法、旧有的掺假义、通晓世情、高端市场、精妙论证，最后到精致生活。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a palm-sized device holds a dozen stacked circuit layers, opened into a turning model on a tablet.
core.cn: 核心意象：掌心大小的设备里叠着十几层电路，在平板上展开成旋转的模型。

branches.en: THE MACHINE: complex construction and precise method.
branches.cn: 机器：复杂构造与精密方法。

branches.en: THE PERSON: social experience and a knowing view of the world.
branches.cn: 人：社会经验与通晓世情的看法。

branches.en: THE TASTE: refined style in food, decor and daily habits.
branches.cn: 品味：食物、陈设与日常习惯中的精致风格。

branches.en: THE OLD CHARGE: the historical sense of something tampered with.
branches.cn: 旧日指控：历史上「被做手脚」的含义。

branches.en: THE MARKET AND THE ARGUMENT: a high-end segment and a subtle case.
branches.cn: 市场与论证：高端区间与精妙的论辩。

intro.en: Sophisticated is a Greek wisdom stem, a Latin verb of tampering, and an English participle ending that still carries both histories.
intro.cn: 这个词是一个希腊「智慧」词干、一个拉丁「做手脚」动词，和一个仍带着两段历史的英语分词词尾。

latinIntro.en: Greek supplies sophos and sophistes; Latin supplies sophisticus and sophisticare, and English builds the participle on the Latin stem.
latinIntro.cn: 希腊语提供了 sophos 与 sophistes；拉丁语提供了 sophisticus 与 sophisticare，英语在拉丁词干上构成分词。

items.example: The root names wisdom.
items.exampleCN: 词根命名智慧。

items.example: The professional figure carries the root.
items.exampleCN: 这一职业身份承载词根。

items.example: The adjective adds argument.
items.exampleCN: 形容词加上论辩色彩。

items.example: Latin borrows the Greek adjective.
items.exampleCN: 拉丁语借入希腊形容词。

items.example: The verb supplies the old charge.
items.exampleCN: 这个动词提供旧日的指控。

items.example: It forms the past participle.
items.exampleCN: 它构成过去分词。

items.example: The word reverses its old charge.
items.exampleCN: 这个词反转了旧日的指控。

items.example: The noun adds a state ending.
items.exampleCN: 名词加上状态词尾。

items.example: It forms unsophisticated, the plain case.
items.exampleCN: 它构成 unsophisticated，即朴素的情形。

derivatives.zh: 由形容词加状态名词词尾构成，义为「精致；老练」
同词干动词与名词，义为「使精巧」与「老于世故者」
由否定前缀加本词构成，义为「单纯质朴的」
由形容词加副词词尾构成，义为「精密地」

definition_zh: 稀缺的；缺乏的；稀少的；罕见的；勉强的
definition_en: existing in too small an amount to meet demand, or found only in small numbers
core_image: 水桶底部只剩薄薄一层水，门外排队的人群一直延伸到街角，门口贴着限购通知
scene: 水站门口的队伍排到街角，桶里的水只剩薄薄一层，管理员在门上贴出限购通知。Clean water became scarce after the pipeline broke.
sceneCN: 这里指水这类基本物资供应不足（第 1 个义项：物资短缺）；句意为管道破裂后，干净的水变得稀缺。图中可辨识物件：排队的人群、见底的水桶、限购通知、街角。

pos.zh: 稀缺的；缺乏的；稀少的；勉强的

derivatives.zh: 由形容词加表示状态的名词词尾构成，义为「稀缺；短缺」
由形容词加副词词尾构成，义为「几乎不；勉强」
由形容词加表示性质的名词词尾构成，义为「稀少」，较少使用

senses.title: Supplies too small for demand
senses.definition: of goods such as water, food or fuel, existing in amounts too small for the people who need them
senses.definitionCN: 指水、食物或燃料等物资的数量低于需求
senses.example: Clean water became scarce after the pipeline broke.
senses.exampleCN: 管道破裂后，干净的水变得稀缺。
senses.why: The French source meant plucked out or thinned away; what has been picked over is no longer plentiful.
senses.whyCN: 法语来源意为「被摘走、被削薄」；被挑过的就不再充足。

senses.title: Resources in limited supply
senses.definition: of natural or economic resources, available in quantities below what is wanted
senses.definitionCN: 指自然或经济资源的可用量低于所需
senses.example: Land is scarce in the old city centre.
senses.exampleCN: 在老城中心，土地很稀缺。
senses.why: Economics uses the word for the basic condition of any limited good.
senses.whyCN: 经济学用这个词描述任何有限物品的基本状况。

senses.title: Rare and therefore valued
senses.definition: found in small numbers and therefore prized
senses.definitionCN: 数量少，因而受珍视
senses.example: First editions are scarce and expensive.
senses.exampleCN: 初版书稀少而昂贵。
senses.why: When supply is thin, price and prestige follow, which is why scarce often sounds like valuable.
senses.whyCN: 供应一薄，价格与声望随之而来，所以这个词常听起来像「珍贵」。

senses.title: A person or chance seldom met
senses.definition: of people or opportunities, appearing rarely
senses.definitionCN: 指人或机会很少出现
senses.example: A chance like this is scarce, so take it now.
senses.exampleCN: 这样的机会很少见，现在就抓住它。
senses.why: The word leaves goods and counts appearances instead.
senses.whyCN: 这个词离开货物，转而计算出现的次数。

senses.title: Barely enough
senses.definition: just sufficient and with no margin to spare
senses.definitionCN: 刚好够用，没有一点余量
senses.example: Jobs were scarce that winter, and every hour mattered.
senses.exampleCN: 那个冬天工作机会很少，每个小时都重要。
senses.why: The adjective can describe a thin margin rather than an absolute shortage.
senses.whyCN: 这个形容词可以描述薄薄的余量，而不只是绝对短缺。

senses.title: The economic condition of scarcity
senses.definition: the state in which limited means must be allocated among unlimited wants
senses.definitionCN: 有限手段需要在无限欲望之间分配的状态
senses.example: The course begins with the problem of scarce resources.
senses.exampleCN: 这门课从资源稀缺这一问题开始。
senses.why: Economics turned the adjective into a formal noun, scarcity, and made it the starting point of the discipline.
senses.whyCN: 经济学把这个形容词变成正式名词「稀缺性」，并把它当作学科的起点。

senses.title: A species found in few places
senses.definition: of a plant or animal, occurring in low numbers or few locations
senses.definitionCN: 指动植物数量少或分布地点少
senses.example: The orchid is scarce in the wild but common in gardens.
senses.exampleCN: 这种兰花在野外稀少，在花园里却常见。
senses.why: Ecology distinguishes scarcity from rarity: a scarce species may still be widespread in small numbers.
senses.whyCN: 生态学把「短缺」与「稀有」分开：稀缺的物种也可能小数量广布。

senses.title: Shortage during a crisis
senses.definition: of goods rationed or hoarded in wartime or disaster
senses.definitionCN: 指战时或灾后被配给或囤积的物资
senses.example: Paper was scarce during the war, so letters were short.
senses.exampleCN: 战争期间纸张紧缺，所以信件都很短。
senses.why: Crisis makes the word concrete: shelves empty and rules appear.
senses.whyCN: 危机让这个词具体化：货架空掉，规则出现。

senses.title: Costly because hard to obtain
senses.definition: of a good whose price is driven up by its short supply
senses.definitionCN: 指价格因供应短缺而被推高的商品
senses.example: Skilled labour is scarce, and wages reflect it.
senses.exampleCN: 熟练劳动力稀缺，工资也反映了这一点。
senses.why: The price is the visible shadow of the missing supply.
senses.whyCN: 价格是供应缺口投下的可见影子。

intro.en: Scarce comes through French from a Latin verb meaning to pluck out: what has been picked out and thinned is no longer plentiful.
intro.cn: 这个词经法语来自拉丁语表示「摘出」的动词：被挑出、被削薄的东西就不再充足。

items.en: carpere meant to pluck, to pick, to gather; it is the root inside the word.
items.cn: carpere 意为「摘、采、收集」，是这个词内部的词根。

items.en: ex- plus carpere gave excerpere, to pluck out or pick out from a larger body.
items.cn: 表示「向外」的前缀加 carpere，构成 excerpere，意为「从整体中摘出、挑出」。

items.en: The Vulgar Latin participle excarpsus meant literally plucked out, and it carried the idea of something thinned or used up.
items.cn: 通俗拉丁语分词 excarpsus 字面意为「被摘出」，带有「被削薄、被用尽」的意思。

items.en: Old French eschars meant sparse or stingy, and the northern form scars passed into English.
items.cn: 古法语 eschars 意为「稀疏的、吝啬的」，北方方言形式 scars 进入英语。

items.en: English borrowed the adjective in the fourteenth century and displaced the older native word for sparse; the exact first date is approximate.
items.cn: 英语在十四世纪借入这个形容词，取代了更早的本族语「稀疏」词；具体首见年份为约数。

items.en: Economics built scarcity on the adjective and made limited supply the central problem of the field.
items.cn: 经济学在形容词基础上构成 scarcity，并把供应有限设为该领域的中心问题。

note.en: The first group shares the root or looks close; the second group names nearby ideas of shortage, and the note separates scarce from rare.
note.cn: 第一组共享词根或形音相近；第二组是邻近的短缺类说法，说明中把 scarce 与 rare 分开。

entries.definition: The noun for a shortage or for the economic condition of limited supply.
entries.definitionCN: 指短缺，或经济学上的供应有限状态。

entries.definition: An adverb meaning barely or almost not at all.
entries.definitionCN: 副词，意为「几乎不、勉强」。

entries.definition: A rare noun for the quality of being scarce.
entries.definitionCN: 指「稀少」性质的一个少用名词。

entries.definition: Frightened; it looks close but comes from a word for terror, not plucking.
entries.definitionCN: 指害怕的；形近，但来自表示「恐惧」的词，而非「摘取」。

entries.definition: The adjective itself, used of goods, resources, chances and species.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词本身，用于货物、资源、机会与物种。

entries.definition: Inherently uncommon in number or occurrence; a rare thing need not be in demand, it is simply not often found.
entries.definitionCN: 指数量或出现本身就不常见；稀有的东西不一定有人需要，只是不常被发现。

entries.definition: Restricted in amount by a rule or limit; it stresses a ceiling rather than a shortage.
entries.definitionCN: 指数量受规则或限度约束；强调上限，而非短缺。

entries.definition: Not enough for a stated need; it judges adequacy rather than market supply.
entries.definitionCN: 指不足以满足某一明确需求；判断是否够用，而非市场供应。

entries.definition: Thinly spread out over an area; it stresses distribution, not quantity.
entries.definitionCN: 指在某区域稀疏分布；强调分布，而非数量。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations use the real plucked-out image, the real French route and the real economics noun.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想使用真实的「摘出」意象、真实的法语路线，以及真实的经济学名词。

normal.en: The root means pluck: a field picked over is a field that has become scarce.
normal.cn: 词根意为「摘」：被摘过一遍的田野，就是变得稀缺的田野。

normal.en: Water, land and first editions can all be scarce, because supply is thinner than demand.
normal.cn: 水、土地与初版书都可能稀缺，因为供应比需求薄。

normal.en: Scarce resources, scarce water and scarce opportunity are three real phrases.
normal.cn: 稀缺资源、缺乏的水与难得的机会是三个真实搭配。

normal.en: Scarcity is the noun, scarcely the adverb, and both come from the same thin supply.
normal.cn: scarcity 是名词，scarcely 是副词，都来自同一份稀薄的供应。

normal.en: Rare means seldom found; scarce means not enough for those who want it.
normal.cn: rare 是「很少见」；scarce 是「不够想要的人分」。

abstract.en: Scarcity is a relationship, not a number: the same amount is plentiful for ten and scarce for a thousand.
abstract.cn: 稀缺是一种关系，而非一个数字：同样的量对十个人充足，对一千个人就稀缺。

abstract.en: A scarce thing becomes valuable, and value can make the scarcity worse.
abstract.cn: 稀缺之物变得有价值，而价值又会加剧稀缺。

abstract.en: The word began as an image of picking and ends as the starting point of economics.
abstract.cn: 这个词始于摘取的意象，最终成为经济学的起点。

examples.en: Fresh vegetables are scarce in the northern villages during winter.
examples.cn: 冬季北方村庄的新鲜蔬菜很稀缺。

examples.en: Accommodation near the campus is scarce and rents are high.
examples.cn: 校园附近的住处稀缺，租金很高。

examples.en: Good data on the species is scarce, so the population estimate remains rough.
examples.cn: 关于该物种的可靠数据很少，因此种群估计仍然粗略。

dict_mnemonic.text: 读作「斯凯尔斯」——被摘过一遍，剩下就稀稀拉拉

root: 来自古法语北方方言 scars「稀疏的、吝啬的」← 古法语 eschars ← 通俗拉丁语 excarpsus「被摘出的」← 拉丁语 excerpere「摘出、挑出」← ex-「向外」+ carpere「摘、采」。十四世纪进入英语，取代本族语的「稀疏」词。来源链清楚，首见年份为约数。

sensesIntro.en: Nine senses run from short supplies of water through resources, prized rarities, rare chances, thin margins, economic scarcity, sparse species, crisis rationing and high prices.
sensesIntro.cn: 九个义项从水的供应不足，经过资源、珍贵稀有物、难得机会、薄余量、经济稀缺、稀少物种、危机配给，最后到高价。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a bucket holds a finger of water, a queue runs to the corner, and a ration notice hangs on the gate.
core.cn: 核心意象：桶里只剩一指深的水，队伍排到街角，门口挂着限购通知。

branches.en: THE SHORT SUPPLY: water, land and wartime goods thinner than demand.
branches.cn: 供应不足：水、土地与战时物资比需求更薄。

branches.en: THE VALUED RARITY: small numbers that raise price and prestige.
branches.cn: 受珍视的稀有：少量供应抬高价格与声望。

branches.en: THE RARE CHANCE: a person or opening seldom met.
branches.cn: 难得机会：很少遇到的人或入口。

branches.en: THE THIN MARGIN: just enough, with nothing to spare.
branches.cn: 薄余量：刚好够，毫无富余。

branches.en: THE FORMAL CONDITION: scarcity in economics and sparse numbers in ecology.
branches.cn: 正式状况：经济学中的稀缺与生态学中的稀疏。

intro.en: Scarce is not built from English pieces; the Latin prefix and plucking root are visible only through the French borrowing.
intro.cn: 这个词不是由英语部件拼成；拉丁前缀与「摘取」词根只有透过法语借词才能看见。

latinIntro.en: Latin supplies carpere, excerpere and the Vulgar Latin participle excarpsus; French supplies eschars and scars.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语提供了 carpere、excerpere 与通俗拉丁语分词 excarpsus；法语提供了 eschars 与 scars。

items.example: It marks taking something out of a whole.
items.exampleCN: 它标记从整体中取出。

items.example: The root names the picking hand.
items.exampleCN: 词根命名采摘的手。
